vkkAFWIjKP.claimed_gains: Competitive with representative WAM and VLA baselines at 0.9B total parameters (0.6B trainable), and V-JEPA latents beat discriminative, reconstructive, and video-understanding alternatives under distribution shift; no margins in the available abstract.
vkkAFWIjKP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it a simple, practical alternative to generator-based world-action models, with controlled, comprehensive experiments in simulation and the real world and gains from action-free predictor pretraining.
vkkAFWIjKP.main_concern: Novelty beyond existing V-JEPA-based world-action models and MoT-style architectures is limited, and the necessity of joint training and the source of pretraining transfer are not isolated.

R8fFxOs6P7.one_liner: A policy-gradient controller learns class-wise loss weights from validation feedback to raise worst-class adversarial IoU in segmentation.
R8fFxOs6P7.problem: Adversarially trained segmentation models show large class-wise robustness disparities, and an adversarial fairness method from classification reduces worst-class and overall robustness, attributed to a mismatch between recall-based difficulty and the IoU objective.
R8fFxOs6P7.method: RL-SAF combines class-level loss aggregation with a policy-gradient controller that adaptively learns class-wise loss weights from validation feedback.
R8fFxOs6P7.key_idea: Treat class-wise loss weights as actions of a policy-gradient controller driven by validation feedback, with class-level loss aggregation matching the IoU objective.
R8fFxOs6P7.evidence: Cityscapes with DeepLabV3 across several attacks including SegPGD, with analyses of class-wise disparities across datasets, architectures, and adversarial training strategies.
R8fFxOs6P7.claimed_gains: Improves adversarial IoU of the most vulnerable classes across all evaluated attacks and preserves robust mIoU under the training attack while trading off part of it under stronger attacks; a review cites SegPGD-3 mIoU 26.78% for SegPGD-AT versus 27.05% for RL-SAF.
R8fFxOs6P7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analysis of class-wise adversarial disparities in segmentation thorough and well motivated, explaining why classification-based fairness methods do not transfer.
R8fFxOs6P7.main_concern: The evaluation is narrow and under-powered: only DeepLabV3 on Cityscapes, apparently single runs without variance, and the benefit of the RL controller over simpler weighting is not established.

Yo9FTxIKBv.one_liner: An LLM agent plans the world and journey while a video world model generates chunks into a geometric spatial memory.
Yo9FTxIKBv.problem: Interactive video world models demand low-level camera and text control from users, and the generated world struggles to stay persistent as exploration proceeds.
Yo9FTxIKBv.method: AgiWorld-Agent keeps a world state and directs exploration, while AgiWorld-WM generates video chunk by chunk and stores it with its geometry in a spatial memory from which the agent updates its world state. Occlusion-aware history selection retrieves past views by surface visibility, and reliability-based memory maintenance prefers reliable geometry.
Yo9FTxIKBv.key_idea: Close a loop between an agent's semantic world state and a shared geometric spatial memory, with visibility-based retrieval and reliability-based maintenance of that memory.
Yo9FTxIKBv.evidence: Quantitative comparison of AgiWorld-WM against seven baselines and memory ablations on fixed ground-truth trajectories; the full agentic system is shown mostly through qualitative examples.
Yo9FTxIKBv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the split between the agent's semantic world state and the video model's geometric memory sensible, and the world-model component technically strong with memory mechanisms addressing concrete failures.
Yo9FTxIKBv.main_concern: The full agentic system is validated only qualitatively on a few scenes, with no aggregate instruction-completion or consistency metrics and no comparison with other agentic world builders.

0MuWXB6VI3.one_liner: Shows RL policies can be recovered from synthetic teacher-labeled inputs, with recovery governed by geometric coverage of the query distribution.
0MuWXB6VI3.problem: It is unclear whether a trained RL policy can be recovered without trajectories, rewards, or valid environment states, and what makes synthetic queries sufficient.
0MuWXB6VI3.method: Students are trained only on teacher-labeled synthetic inputs; matched subspace interventions vary excitation of teacher-sensitive directions, and orthogonal thickening varies ambient support. Theory ties covariance mismatch to deployment error.
0MuWXB6VI3.key_idea: Recovery depends on exciting teacher-sensitive directions and on sufficient variance outside the dominant sensitive subspace, not on physical realism of the queries.
0MuWXB6VI3.evidence: Control tasks including Humanoid-v5, Hopper, and Ant with SAC and discrete-action ReLU policies, subspace-intervention experiments, theory on covariance mismatch, and a synthetic-only pilot of inverse-covariance coverage.
0MuWXB6VI3.claimed_gains: On Humanoid-v5, 0.10-scale orthogonal noise raises recovery from 8.1% to 73.7% with almost unchanged sensitivity overlap.
0MuWXB6VI3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the synthetic-only recovery setting interesting and credit the controlled subspace and thickening experiments for showing that both directional sensitivity and broader coverage affect recovery.
0MuWXB6VI3.main_concern: The covariance experiments change variances and correlations together, so no diagonal-covariance control separates their effects, and some reported recovery values are inconsistent across tables.

Lg1FLMXfR8.one_liner: Marginalizes over all generation orders of semantic and collaborative item IDs using a canonical-state lattice and dynamic programming.
Lg1FLMXfR8.problem: Semantic and collaborative ID chains have no inherent cross-chain order, yet autoregressive generation needs a total order, and the arbitrary serialization affects recommendation performance.
Lg1FLMXfR8.method: LatticeRec treats cross-identifier serialization as a latent variable. Partial generations are represented by canonical states determined only by the revealed prefixes of both chains, forming a lattice that allows exact marginalization over orders by dynamic programming, plus coverage-aware training so supervision does not concentrate on a few paths.
Lg1FLMXfR8.key_idea: Merge interleavings that reveal the same prefixes into one shared predictive state, so dynamic programming sums over all valid orders without enumerating paths.
Lg1FLMXfR8.evidence: Three benchmarks (including Instruments and Games), comparisons with fixed and random orders, marginal versus max aggregation at inference, and component ablations.
Lg1FLMXfR8.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports only that experiments on three benchmarks show effectiveness); a review notes a small Games NDCG@10 gain from 0.0533 to 0.0536.
Lg1FLMXfR8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear, with controlled evidence that generation order matters and canonical-state sharing giving exact marginalization without path enumeration.
Lg1FLMXfR8.main_concern: The independent benefit of marginalization is unclear: the best settings use coverage weight 1 (equal to uniform-path supervision), some gains are small, and training compute is not matched to the sampled-path baseline.

kEZLqIt4Gf.one_liner: Neural predictors built from radial transformations whose sublevel sets are exact unions of ellipsoids, enabling closed-form preimage optimization.
kEZLqIt4Gf.problem: Expressive neural predictors have no explicit preimage representation, so characterizing and optimizing over the inputs meeting a target level is expensive.
kEZLqIt4Gf.method: TRIO factorizes the preimage: the forward model uses nonlinear radial transformations (including neural networks) that reduce, under inversion, to a single scalar radius, giving simple geometric level sets. For linear objectives this yields a closed-form global solution, and a universal approximation theorem covers forward and backward approximation.
kEZLqIt4Gf.key_idea: Take the minimum of radial components so each sublevel set is an exact union of ellipsoids, making preimage optimization tractable by construction.
kEZLqIt4Gf.evidence: Two 2D benchmarks, a backbone-size sensitivity study, and a 5-variable AC power-flow application with Pandapower, plus a universal approximation theorem.
kEZLqIt4Gf.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract; a review cites downstream optimization time staying flat across a 400x range of radial-backbone sizes.
kEZLqIt4Gf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the structural idea clean, with an exactness guarantee independent of training and a closed-form global solution for linear objectives.
kEZLqIt4Gf.main_concern: Experiments are low-dimensional (2D benchmarks and 5 variables) and the approximation rate O(Q^{-1/d}) suggests a curse of dimensionality, leaving scalability and multi-output constraints unaddressed.

TUrOPXq7D7.one_liner: Proves, under standard complexity assumptions, that no truly subquadratic algorithm gives any nontrivial uniform approximation of softmax attention.
TUrOPXq7D7.problem: Known lower bounds rule out fast near-exact attention but leave open whether any efficient algorithm has even a modest uniform approximation guarantee.
TUrOPXq7D7.method: The paper reduces from the hardness of approximate closest pair to show lower bounds for additive and relative approximation, then extends them to KV-cache preprocessing and to sparse retrieval of keys receiving substantial attention.
TUrOPXq7D7.key_idea: Use dummy keys so the normalized attention output becomes an almost-binary test, transferring closest-pair hardness to fixed-error attention approximation.
TUrOPXq7D7.evidence: Theory only: conditional lower-bound theorems (for example Theorems 3.7, 4.1, and 5.1) under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions.
TUrOPXq7D7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the results close the gap between near-exact and coarse approximation hardness and extend it to KV-cache preprocessing and sparse retrieval.
TUrOPXq7D7.main_concern: The worst-case hardness relies on adversarial inputs and constants that depend on the target speedup, so relevance to real attention and the new contribution over prior closest-pair reductions are unclear.

hJEANWvAwR.one_liner: LLM-agent system for ML on physics time series with composable capabilities, multi-layer scientific-validity checks, and resource-aware exploration.
hJEANWvAwR.problem: Score-driven LLM agents can exploit shortcuts, trigger mode collapse, or game the evaluation, producing models with high scores that are scientifically invalid.
hJEANWvAwR.method: SIDERIUS combines contract-defined composable capabilities for orchestration and human-in-the-loop, a multi-layer scientific evaluation protocol separating valid models from unhealthy or gaming ones, and resource-aware exploration for expensive scientific ML.
hJEANWvAwR.key_idea: Gate agent-proposed models through a layered scientific-validity rubric instead of a single score, while routing work through contract-defined composable capabilities.
hJEANWvAwR.evidence: TIDMAD benchmark against a GPT orchestrator using the Codex coding agent, plus three additional physics time-series datasets and a cost analysis.
hJEANWvAwR.claimed_gains: On TIDMAD, reaches a 63.8% valid-model proposal rate and a best valid denoising score of 2.744, versus 1.6% and -0.647 for the same GPT model with the Codex coding agent.
hJEANWvAwR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reward hacking on physics denoising a real, well-illustrated problem and credit the modular design and the Codex comparison under the same GPT model.
hJEANWvAwR.main_concern: The evaluation rubric was refined on the same campaign logs used for the main results and was not independently validated (no blinded adjudication or agreement metrics), and component contributions are not isolated.

9khJgK6p1C.one_liner: Constructs synchronous asymmetric binary Hopfield networks with superpolynomially many noise-robust limit cycles of superpolynomial period.
9khJgK6p1C.problem: High-capacity storage of long sequences in classical synchronous asymmetric Hopfield networks has remained a challenge.
9khJgK6p1C.method: A block-cyclic construction, built from combinatorics, number theory, and opinion-dynamics analysis, lets n neurons support exp(Omega(n/(log n)^2)) limit-cycle attractors, each with period exp(Omega(sqrt(n)/log n)) and robust to flip probability up to 1/2 - o(1).
9khJgK6p1C.key_idea: Compose disjoint block cycles of different lengths, so the full network's period is the least common multiple of the block cycle lengths.
9khJgK6p1C.evidence: Theorems with proofs in the classical binary, synchronous model, plus finite-size experiments on synthetic networks (recovery tests mostly initialized from constant states).
9khJgK6p1C.claimed_gains: n neurons support exp(Omega(n/(log n)^2)) distinct limit-cycle attractors, each with period exp(Omega(sqrt(n)/log n)) and robust to noise with flip probability up to 1/2 - o(1).
9khJgK6p1C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper mathematically solid, clearly written, and interesting for linking architecture to attractor complexity, with an intuitive block-cyclic explanation of long periods.
9khJgK6p1C.main_concern: Novelty over known symmetric networks with exponentially many fixed points is unclear, the link to Dale's law is weak, and experiments do not directly show retrieval of distinct non-constant long-period cycles.

F0zMVaI13l.one_liner: Adds one per-rollout latent with encoder, KL, and energy-score loss to streaming flow for probabilistic forecasting in physical time.
F0zMVaI13l.problem: Streaming flow learns a deterministic velocity field, so it gives only one future trajectory for a fixed initial state and observation history, even when several futures are plausible.
F0zMVaI13l.method: VSF learns a latent distribution conditioned on the dynamics, with one latent per rollout, an encoder with KL regularization, and an energy-score reconstruction, while generating in physical time to keep one velocity evaluation per transition.
F0zMVaI13l.key_idea: Sample one latent per rollout to condition a physical-time velocity field, so different latents give different futures at no extra per-step cost.
F0zMVaI13l.evidence: Deterministic and stochastic dynamical systems (double pendulum, Rossler, Lorenz), rollouts exceeding 1,000 steps, bifurcating dynamics, and plug-in use in JEPA-based world models.
F0zMVaI13l.claimed_gains: Superior predictive accuracy and distributional fidelity, long-horizon rollouts exceeding 1,000 steps, and improved goal-directed success in JEPA-based world models; no numbers in the available abstract.
F0zMVaI13l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, well explained, and easy to plug into streaming flow, with long-horizon evaluation showing accuracy and calibration at low cost.
F0zMVaI13l.main_concern: Novelty over streaming flow is limited since the latent-variable and energy-score components are standard, and the test systems are low-dimensional with synthetic hidden-parameter uncertainty that matches the single-latent design.

OF4BXL8CpL.one_liner: A cross-attention transformer with directional masks and orthogonal decoders splits inter-regional neural signals into leading and lagging streams.
OF4BXL8CpL.problem: Feedforward and feedback signals are superimposed with temporal offsets across brain regions, making directed inter-regional communication hard to interpret in multi-region recordings.
OF4BXL8CpL.method: BiXformer is a bidirectional cross-attention transformer that decomposes inter-regional communication into temporally leading and lagging streams using directionally masked attention, recovering low-dimensional directed latent dynamics and communication delays.
OF4BXL8CpL.key_idea: Enforce temporal constraints inside attention heads through directional masks, so heads expose lag preferences and the two streams decode through orthogonal decoders.
OF4BXL8CpL.evidence: Synthetic data with known delays, neural-behavioral recordings, and simultaneous S1-M1 recordings during a movement task, with comparisons including DLAG and MR-LFADS.
OF4BXL8CpL.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing methods in accuracy and speed on synthetic data with known delays; no numbers in the available abstract.
OF4BXL8CpL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the explicit decomposition via directional masks interpretable, with accurate recovery of latents and delays on synthetic data and extensive evaluation on real recordings.
OF4BXL8CpL.main_concern: Synthetic validation is limited to stationary Gaussian processes with linear mixing and one dataset for baselines, and lead-lag signatures may arise without communication since no trial-shuffle control or identifiability test is reported.

K9LsbxklIM.one_liner: One-step MeanFlow posterior sampler for noisy linear inverse problems using a measurement-adapted Gaussian source.
K9LsbxklIM.problem: Diffusion and flow-matching posterior samplers need tens to thousands of network evaluations, and one-step MeanFlow leaves no intermediate steps at which to enforce measurement consistency.
K9LsbxklIM.method: SNaP starts the flow from a Gaussian source whose mean and anisotropic covariance are set by the measurement operator, observation, and noise level, anchoring well-measured directions while keeping variation where measurements are weak. The authors show the exact conditional flow transports this source to the true posterior.
K9LsbxklIM.key_idea: Choose the MeanFlow source distribution from the measurement operator and noise level so a single network evaluation yields posterior samples.
K9LsbxklIM.evidence: Natural-image restoration (CelebA) and multi-coil MRI (fastMRI), with a synthetic Gaussian-mixture experiment and source ablations.
K9LsbxklIM.claimed_gains: One network evaluation per draw, 30 to 2250x faster than iterative samplers.
K9LsbxklIM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the measurement-adapted source well motivated and simple, with diverse high-quality one-step samples and better calibrated spread than alternatives on CelebA.
K9LsbxklIM.main_concern: The comparison is incomplete or unfair: SNaP trains a separate supervised model per operator while baselines are zero-shot, few-step solvers such as CM4IR and LATINO are missing, and fastMRI draw variance appears too low.

L4NKzzNhhq.one_liner: Proves MCR^2 can reach near-optimal coding yet fail completely under correlation reversal, even when a perfectly stable feature is available.
L4NKzzNhhq.problem: MCR^2 yields structured representations and white-box architectures, but its behavior under distribution shift is unclear and it can completely fail.
L4NKzzNhhq.method: The paper builds an analyzable two-dimensional, two-class model where a representation based on an unstable environmental feature attains the global coding optimum but fails after correlation reversal, and it examines directly adding an invariance principle from invariant risk methods (abstract cut off).
L4NKzzNhhq.key_idea: A representation using only an environmental feature can match the global coding optimum while correlation reversal sends prediction error near 100%, because MCR^2 cannot tell stable from spurious features.
L4NKzzNhhq.evidence: Theoretical lemmas and theorems in a d=K=2 balanced-class model, with a limited Waterbirds experiment using ResNet-18 on a single seed.
L4NKzzNhhq.claimed_gains: not stated (the theoretical claim is that coding quality can be arbitrarily close to optimal while prediction error is arbitrarily close to 100%)
L4NKzzNhhq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theoretical characterization precise and clearly presented, formalizing why MCR^2 cannot separate stable from spurious correlations, with limitations stated transparently.
L4NKzzNhhq.main_concern: The failure is not specific to MCR^2, since cross-entropy shows the same near-optimal reliance on spurious features, and the analysis is idealized with little empirical support.

WGbmwrq4xn.one_liner: Adds a latent multi-stream memory to VLA models, pretrained by history reconstruction and progress estimation, then fine-tuned with the policy.
WGbmwrq4xn.problem: Conditioning policies on all past observations invites spurious shortcuts and latency, while curated memories (recent frames, keyframes, summaries) require task-specific priors about what to remember.
WGbmwrq4xn.method: IMPRINT compresses multiple streams (observations, actions, proprioception) into a latent memory updated incrementally at inference. Stage one supervises the memory to reconstruct past streams and estimate task progress, and stage two fine-tunes memory and VLA end to end on action prediction.
WGbmwrq4xn.key_idea: Pretrain a compact latent memory to reconstruct multiple history streams and estimate task progress, without prescribing what to remember, then adapt it jointly with the policy.
WGbmwrq4xn.evidence: Two simulation benchmarks (including RMBench and RoboCasa) and three real-world tasks, with ablations on memory capacity, input streams, training objectives, and adaptation strategies.
WGbmwrq4xn.claimed_gains: Improves average success over the base VLA by at least 26 percentage points; a latency of 122.8 ms per action chunk is reported as the lowest among the memory baselines compared.
WGbmwrq4xn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the encoding-versus-learning framing clear and the gains promising on memory-dependent tasks without hurting non-memory tasks, supported by extensive ablations and representation analyses.
WGbmwrq4xn.main_concern: The latency and baseline comparisons are not like-for-like (EventVLA and MemoryVLA numbers come from prior work on different backbones), and there is no compute-matched end-to-end baseline for the two-stage training.

er9unpQDiP.one_liner: Learns a summary balancing treatment groups against a held-out proxy block, then adjusts for it to estimate causal effects.
er9unpQDiP.problem: Proxy-based causal inference either designates proxy roles and solves an ill-posed inverse problem that is hard with high-dimensional proxies, or uses a latent-variable model that leaves bias when the latent variable does not match the hidden confounder.
er9unpQDiP.method: PROBE learns a low-dimensional summary of the covariates and proxies that makes treatment groups comparable, with a held-out proxy block used to audit balance, and then adjusts for that summary. When the valid held-out block is unknown, it aggregates estimates across proxy splits by plurality vote.
er9unpQDiP.key_idea: Learn a summary of covariates and retained proxies that makes a held-out proxy block independent of treatment, then adjust for that summary instead of solving a bridge equation.
er9unpQDiP.evidence: Identification theory and finite-sample guarantees, with experiments on low-dimensional, high-dimensional, and image proxies and on real-world data.
er9unpQDiP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the approach for avoiding designated proxy roles, bridge equations, and latent-variable models, and for a thorough analysis of identification, imperfect balance, and aggregation.
er9unpQDiP.main_concern: Identification relies on a valid held-out proxy block and on correct estimates forming the plurality, with limited stress tests for cases where several invalid splits agree.

D54Tq2ULjl.one_liner: Multi-agent pipeline that turns published papers into executable research environments with automated evaluators for recursive self-improvement.
D54Tq2ULjl.problem: Building challenging research environments with reliable evaluation for recursive self-improvement depends on domain experts, which limits scale and disciplinary coverage.
D54Tq2ULjl.method: Three agents coordinate construction, reproduction, and review to produce tasks with automated evaluators, and each paper's method is independently reimplemented to set a baseline score. The result is 210 environments across 18 fields, 90 of them reviewed by independent human domain experts.
D54Tq2ULjl.key_idea: Separate authoring, independent reproduction, and review agents, so each paper's reimplemented method sets the baseline score and a reproduction must beat the starting solution for an environment to pass.
D54Tq2ULjl.evidence: Ratings from human experts and agent judges on the environments, and four models run over 3 successive attempts on 120 environments, each attempt inheriting prior code and notes with fixed model weights.
D54Tq2ULjl.claimed_gains: At least one model improves after the first attempt in 83% of environments, and models outperform the reproduced paper methods in 67 of the 120 environments.
D54Tq2ULjl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sourcing environments automatically from the literature addresses a real bottleneck, that 210 environments across 18 domains is meaningful scale, and that the staged construction with reproduction gating is sensible.
D54Tq2ULjl.main_concern: Held-out data leakage (22 of 480 chains) stays in the headline results, and the baseline definition is circular because the starting solution can be tuned to make reproductions pass.

A7LRs2y204.one_liner: Trains a sequence model to emit several spherical caps (center, radius) that cover a user's future items cheaply.
A7LRs2y204.problem: Retrieval must decide where to place query vectors and how far to search, and query placement suffers sampling error from limited history and drift error from changing user interests.
A7LRs2y204.method: Cosine-similarity retrieval is framed as searching spherical caps whose cost is cap area, so multi-query retrieval becomes a geometric covering problem. A model learns multiple regions from user histories, each with a query center and an angular radius, trained to cover future target items while minimizing total region.
A7LRs2y204.key_idea: Parameterize each retrieval region as a spherical cap with a learned center and angular radius, and train to cover future items while minimizing total cap area.
A7LRs2y204.evidence: Theoretical analysis of retrieval cost with multiple regions and offline experiments on five datasets against single- and multi-interest baselines; reviews also mention an internal short-video dataset and an online serving section.
A7LRs2y204.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the geometric covering framing, which links cosine-similarity retrieval to spherical-cap area, and the joint learning of query centers and radii to trade off coverage against retrieval cost.
A7LRs2y204.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty and a theory-experiment gap, since the theorems assume covering a future item set while evaluation holds out one item per user, and the method does not always beat baselines.

YH95kuGYdt.one_liner: Refines a merged model via anchor-regularized Bayesian linear regression with closed-form updates and Bayesian-optimized module-wise hyperparameters.
YH95kuGYdt.problem: Existing merging methods already produce strong merged models that could serve as priors, but they are not refined further using that prior.
YH95kuGYdt.method: ReForge is a bilevel framework: the inner level gives a closed-form MAP estimate per module from unlabeled calibration activations with an anchor-centered prior, and the outer level uses Bayesian optimization to select regularization strengths and assembly scales on held-out validation data. A calibration-free variant replaces activation statistics with task-vector Grams.
YH95kuGYdt.key_idea: Treat the existing merged model as the prior mean of a per-module Bayesian linear regression solved in closed form, with Bayesian optimization setting regularization strengths and assembly scales.
YH95kuGYdt.evidence: Benchmarks with up to 20-task merging in vision and 5-task merging in language, compared against plug-and-play anchors such as TA, WUDI-Merging, TSV, and ISO-CTS, plus appendix control experiments.
YH95kuGYdt.claimed_gains: On 20-task ViT-B/32, ReForge improves the strongest evaluated baseline, ISO-CTS, from 77.6% to 82.8% in the calibration-assisted setting and to 81.5% in the calibration-free setting.
YH95kuGYdt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note consistent gains across anchor methods, architectures, and task counts in vision and language, and see closed-form refinement of an existing merged model as clean and practical.
YH95kuGYdt.main_concern: Reviewers doubt whether gains come from the method or from extra validation-guided tuning, since anchor rescaling alone already lifts accuracy from 77.6% to 80.5%, and they flag overlap with RegMean-style regression.

EYa8WSk9aA.one_liner: Diffusion model for inorganic crystals that represents oxidation states and enforces charge neutrality with a finite-state-automaton output layer.
EYa8WSk9aA.problem: Existing crystal generative models can produce charge-neutral oxidation-state assignments but poorly reproduce the distributions of oxidation states observed in synthesised materials.
EYa8WSk9aA.method: OxiGen represents oxidation states explicitly during diffusion-based generation, treating each atom as an element-plus-oxidation-state species. A structured output layer with exact inference over a finite-state automaton enforces global charge neutrality by construction.
EYa8WSk9aA.key_idea: Replace elements with (element, oxidation-state) species so charge neutrality becomes a linear integer constraint, enforced exactly by a finite-state-automaton structured output layer.
EYa8WSk9aA.evidence: Evaluation against existing crystal generation models on LeMat-GenBench, including under property conditioning.
EYa8WSk9aA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the oxidation-state representation and exact charge-neutral output layer clearly motivated and effective, and praise the standardized LeMat-GenBench comparison.
EYa8WSk9aA.main_concern: The claim that the structured output layer transfers to other generative models is not demonstrated, a classifier-free-guidance baseline for charge neutrality is missing, and the ICSD data requires a license.

mOWODLFvAk.one_liner: Benchmark for offline multi-agent robotic manipulation with controlled data constructions varying role, temporal, and skill composition.
mOWODLFvAk.problem: Task performance and overall dataset quality alone do not reveal how the mix of coordination experiences in an offline dataset affects what agents can learn.
mOWODLFvAk.method: RoboMARL-Bench provides 65 task configurations, 7 rule-defined interaction structures, and 8 controlled data constructions spanning the source, episode, role, temporal, and skill layers. This enables matched-budget comparisons within the same task while varying how experience is collected and organized.
mOWODLFvAk.key_idea: Construct offline datasets at source, episode, role, temporal, and skill layers under a matched transition budget, so data composition varies while the task stays fixed.
mOWODLFvAk.evidence: Extensive evaluations of current offline multi-agent RL methods across tasks, interaction structures, and data constructions; reviews add results averaged over five seeds on two physics platforms with a real-robot interface.
mOWODLFvAk.claimed_gains: not stated; methods exceed the recorded data level on only about half of the tasks collected by suboptimal policies.
mOWODLFvAk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating data composition as an explicit experimental variable, with role-assignment and controller-switching constructions at matched budgets, is well motivated and yields a useful benchmark resource.
mOWODLFvAk.main_concern: Reviewers question whether findings are confounded or incremental, since fixed-step controller switching may make ordering effects reflect source share, quality labels are uncalibrated, and sim-to-real correlation is not established.

cbxfdbHypL.one_liner: Selective framework that repairs, certifies, or abstains on prompts, separating center certification from neighborhood robustness and response safety.
cbxfdbHypL.problem: Prompt repair can recover benign requests rejected by an input safety gate, but accepting a repaired prompt does not establish robustness to nearby edits or safety of the generated response.
cbxfdbHypL.method: SCORE specializes a likelihood-ratio transfer envelope for fixed, positive categorical smoothing supports and maximizes it exactly over small candidate-set Hamming balls. It tracks center certification, Hamming-neighborhood robustness, and downstream response safety as separate quantities.
cbxfdbHypL.key_idea: Maximize a likelihood-ratio transfer envelope exactly over small candidate-set Hamming balls to certify repaired prompts under randomized smoothing, kept separate from response safety.
cbxfdbHypL.evidence: Held-out evaluations on 606 unsafe prompts routed to repair and 313 rejected benign prompts, development kernel and semantic-support analyses, and two direct Gemma 3 adaptive runs.
cbxfdbHypL.claimed_gains: Branch-and-bound and beam proposal policies certify 215 and 66 of 606 centers but neither certifies a repaired prompt at Hamming radius one, and a dual-gate policy releases 34 of 313 rejected benign prompts and certifies none at radius one.
cbxfdbHypL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the careful separation of center certification, neighborhood robustness, and downstream response safety, the candid negative results, and the broad evaluation across benchmarks, gates, models, and adaptive attacks.
cbxfdbHypL.main_concern: Reviewers say the theory largely adapts known randomized-smoothing and Neyman-Pearson techniques and guarantees only input-classifier stability under limited substitutions, while the paper is dense with no released code or runtime evidence.

WIgQUeXY6v.one_liner: Adapts EEG foundation models by directly predicting event intervals as a set instead of per-window classification and post-hoc merging.
WIgQUeXY6v.problem: Pretrained biosignal foundation models are almost universally adapted through per-window classifiers whose outputs must be thresholded, smoothed, and merged into events after the fact, which limits event-level quality.
WIgQUeXY6v.method: SPAN maps tokens from heterogeneous biosignal backbones into a shared physical-time representation and directly predicts event intervals using multiscale temporal features, anchor-conditioned queries, and duration-dependent attention.
WIgQUeXY6v.key_idea: Replace the per-window dense classifier with a temporal set-prediction head over a shared physical-time token representation, predicting event class, onset, and offset directly.
WIgQUeXY6v.evidence: A paired protocol fixing pretrained initialization, training data, and event scorer compares SPAN with dense per-token fine-tuning across six public EEG foundation-model backbones, four tasks, and three seeds, plus a plain set decoder comparison.
WIgQUeXY6v.claimed_gains: SPAN improves test event F1 at IoU>0.5 in all 72 seed-matched comparisons, with average gains of 4.5--8.3 percentage points per task.
WIgQUeXY6v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paired evaluation across six backbones, four tasks, and three seeds is careful and shows consistent event-F1 gains from changing the adaptation interface.
WIgQUeXY6v.main_concern: The dense baseline lacks cross-window temporal context and multi-label outputs, and SPAN differs from the plain set decoder in width and losses, so the gain is not cleanly attributed to set prediction.

2o0NDciBjX.one_liner: Adaptive regulation of GCL training, driven by contrastive improvement and representation drift, to curb overfitting that erodes structural information.
2o0NDciBjX.problem: Excessive optimization of the graph contrastive objective degrades the learned representations because the encoder progressively loses structural information, which reduces downstream discriminability (contrastive overfitting).
2o0NDciBjX.method: PARE (Progress-Adaptive REgulation) is an adaptive training strategy that plugs into existing GCL methods; reviews describe it as using contrastive improvement and representation drift without downstream labels or encoder changes. The paper pairs it with theoretical and empirical analysis of the overfitting mechanism.
2o0NDciBjX.key_idea: Adapt contrastive training using the progress signals of contrastive improvement and representation drift, rather than optimizing the InfoNCE objective to convergence.
2o0NDciBjX.evidence: Theoretical analysis of the InfoNCE optimum and experiments across various GCL methods; reviews cite six datasets, nine InfoNCE-based GCL methods, and controlled SBM experiments.
2o0NDciBjX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the contrastive-overfitting finding is clear and important, and that PARE is simple, broadly applicable, and evaluated extensively.
2o0NDciBjX.main_concern: PARE gives little gain over the Oracle early-stopped baseline, and it is unclear whether it mitigates structural degeneration or just acts as an adaptive learning-rate schedule.

deMIL5Ii4b.one_liner: Link-prediction model representing nodes as simplex compositions over archetypes, with per-archetype edge channels that serve as built-in explanations.
deMIL5Ii4b.problem: Most graph models represent edges through opaque similarity functions, giving limited insight into how the latent memberships of two nodes combine to produce or inhibit an interaction.
deMIL5Ii4b.method: Nodes are simplex-valued compositions over learned archetypes, and each archetype defines an edge channel combining the pair's shared membership in that archetype with their Aitchison agreement over the remaining archetypes. The channel values jointly determine edge probability and, after normalization, form a compositional representation of the edge.
deMIL5Ii4b.key_idea: Define per-archetype edge channels from shared membership plus Aitchison agreement on remaining archetypes, so the quantities that predict an edge also explain it by construction.
deMIL5Ii4b.evidence: Theory showing the channels retain relational information lost by global membership overlap and full compositional distance and support exact counterfactual reasoning; reviews cite evaluation of predictive accuracy, synthetic archetype recovery, semantic alignment, and interventions.
deMIL5Ii4b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is coherent, with the same archetype channels driving both prediction and explanation, and that the evaluation covers accuracy, archetype recovery, semantic alignment, and interventions.
deMIL5Ii4b.main_concern: Reviewers question the interpretability claim because channel meanings are assigned after the fact by humans, and note that the theory is largely immediate algebra and predictive gains are marginal (ablations differ by at most 0.009 AUC).

FuJuhMPdGa.one_liner: Benchmark separating current-state accuracy, retention of valid facts, and forbidden-value emission when LLMs revoke facts in context.
FuJuhMPdGa.problem: A language model can comply with an in-context request to revoke a fact on a direct query while losing valid neighboring information or later emitting the invalid value.
FuJuhMPdGa.method: RevokeBench contains ERASE, REPLACE, and SUPERSEDE state transitions with paired instruction and physically edited contexts. It scores current-state accuracy, retention of valid facts, and literal forbidden-value emission as separate obligations.
FuJuhMPdGa.key_idea: Compare instruction-mediated revocation against physically edited (canonical) contexts, scoring current-state accuracy, retained utility, and forbidden-value emission as three separate obligations.
FuJuhMPdGa.evidence: 960 test episodes in a two-checkpoint confirmatory study, a separately specified ten-checkpoint panel, human judgments, an external memory-operation bridge, no-revocation controls, and Qwen3-8B attention interventions and suffix recomputation.
FuJuhMPdGa.claimed_gains: In the ten-checkpoint panel, instruction-mediated revocation has 2.31 and 12.92 percentage points lower same-entity retention on IID and OOD splits and 16.47 and 25.12 points higher macro forbidden-value emission than canonical editing, while none of four pre-specified confirmatory contrasts survives Holm correction.
FuJuhMPdGa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating current-state accuracy, retention, and forbidden-value emission is a useful way to evaluate in-context revocation, and that the study is careful and transparent, including reporting failed confirmatory tests.
FuJuhMPdGa.main_concern: Reviewers say canonical editing is treated as an implicit gold standard without enough analysis of its own errors, the forbidden-value metric counts mentions as emission, and the writing and metric definitions need work.

S8KOiI0zGS.one_liner: Supervised neural model for agglomerative clustering aligned with the Lance-Williams recurrence, learning merge rules with efficient, size-generalizing inference.
S8KOiI0zGS.problem: It is often unclear which linkage merge rule suits a given dataset or task, and neural approaches that learn from data often lose the efficiency and size generalization of classical algorithms.
S8KOiI0zGS.method: NN-Linkage learns task-specific, locally dependent merge rules while keeping the recursive structure and efficient inference of classical linkage algorithms. Paired with a transformer encoding, it can also approximate globally dependent rules such as robust single linkage.
S8KOiI0zGS.key_idea: Use recursive merge embeddings processed by fixed-size networks aligned with the Lance-Williams recurrence, so classical linkages are special cases of the learned merge function.
S8KOiI0zGS.evidence: Proofs that NN-Linkage is a universal approximator for continuous linkage functions and exactly implements any symmetric constant-coefficient LW recurrence across all input sizes, plus experiments on real-world applications and a rings-and-disks task.
S8KOiI0zGS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Lance-Williams-aligned design is well motivated, with a meaningful theoretical contribution and demonstrated size generalization.
S8KOiI0zGS.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited experimental validation, missing ablations, and missing comparisons with other neural methods and with classical clustering in runtime.

XRNcmbQebj.one_liner: Training-free prompting that repeats the image-question pair so every token attends to the full input under causal attention.
XRNcmbQebj.problem: Under causal attention in current VLMs, whichever modality comes first is encoded under partial observation of the input, uninformed by the rest of the multimodal context.
XRNcmbQebj.method: Second-Look Prompting (SLP) repeats the image-question pair in the input, so in the repeated copy every visual and textual token can attend to the complete input. The added visual tokens also contribute computation beyond re-exposing the image.
XRNcmbQebj.key_idea: Duplicate the image-question pair in the prompt so the second copy is encoded with full-context attention, and the extra visual tokens act as a prefill scratchpad.
XRNcmbQebj.evidence: Evaluation on 12 benchmarks across nine open-source models (3B-72B) and three proprietary frontier models, with attention analysis and scratchpad probing of the mechanism.
XRNcmbQebj.claimed_gains: SLP improves the overall average score of every evaluated model across 12 benchmarks, with gains reaching 5.6 points for Gemini 3 Flash on MATH-Vision.
XRNcmbQebj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple to apply, clearly motivated, and evaluated across many model families and benchmarks, with rebuttal controls supporting the role of the extra visual block.
XRNcmbQebj.main_concern: Reviewers say average gains are modest relative to the cost of repeating the image input, the mechanism evidence covers limited models and benchmarks, and the method is incremental over prompt repetition.

mg1dsg9gsE.one_liner: KV eviction scoring entries by contrasting attention under the actual query with attention under a generic proxy query.
mg1dsg9gsE.problem: Attention scores mix query-relevant and query-invariant components, so under a limited KV budget the shared patterns can bias selection toward entries less relevant to the current query.
mg1dsg9gsE.method: DeltaKV scores cached entries by contrasting attention under the actual query with attention under a generic proxy query, which discounts shared structure and emphasizes query-specific changes, with minimal computational overhead.
mg1dsg9gsE.key_idea: Subtract proxy-query attention from actual-query attention to rank cached KV entries, removing the query-invariant component shared across queries.
mg1dsg9gsE.evidence: Experiments on LongBench-E, RULER, and MileBench across increasing compression ratios against competing eviction methods.
mg1dsg9gsE.claimed_gains: Across the three benchmarks, evicting 90% of KV entries costs less than 7% relative performance, and with only 2% of the original KV cache DeltaKV retains over 70% of full-cache performance.
mg1dsg9gsE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free, and motivated by evidence that attention is largely shared across queries, and that it retains most performance at 90% eviction.
mg1dsg9gsE.main_concern: The subtraction is not isolated from pooling, since DeltaKV uses kernel size 32 versus 5 for SnapKV and Figure 6 shows pooling strongly affects RULER, so a matched no-subtraction control is missing.

b20IFhqpuz.one_liner: Two-stage soft context compression training: distill on teacher-correct questions, then use reinforcement learning on teacher-failed ones.
b20IFhqpuz.problem: Distilling a compressed RAG model from a full-context teacher reinforces the teacher's errors when it is wrong, and teacher imitation gives no signal for improving beyond the teacher.
b20IFhqpuz.method: DEX-Comp's Pure Distillation stage learns only from teacher-correct questions, and its Hard Exploration stage applies outcome-based reinforcement learning (GRPO, per reviews) to teacher-failed questions to directly optimize answer correctness.
b20IFhqpuz.key_idea: Allocate teacher-correct questions to distillation and teacher-failed questions to outcome-reward reinforcement learning, so imitation avoids teacher errors and exploration targets them.
b20IFhqpuz.evidence: Five open-domain QA benchmarks with retrieval depths from top-5 to top-30, plus additional datasets and backbones, against compression baselines and untuned full-context RAG.
b20IFhqpuz.claimed_gains: At 16x compression DEX-Comp outperforms all evaluated compression baselines and surpasses the untuned full-context RAG model in average accuracy, while reducing time-to-first-token by 4.4x--23.7x.
b20IFhqpuz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the teacher-correctness-based split between distillation and exploration is well motivated and empirically supported, and that compressed RL training and lower time-to-first-token give practical benefits.
b20IFhqpuz.main_concern: The claim of surpassing full-context RAG relies on an untuned baseline, since full-context RL reaches 76.78% versus 72.54% for DEX-Comp at top-5, and baselines lack the same gold-answer or RL treatment.

a4j6KMRWSL.one_liner: Training-free agent context compression: soft tokens for context the model's recurrent state has absorbed, hard tokens for exact values.
a4j6KMRWSL.problem: Accumulated contexts of long-horizon agents raise computational cost and obscure key evidence, and external compressors that rewrite context as shorter hard-token sequences may not align with the LLM's evolving representation and are lossy.
a4j6KMRWSL.method: ASTC uses the native recurrent dynamics of hybrid Gated Delta Network (GDN)-attention models to determine already-absorbed information, carries it forward as agentic soft tokens, and retains exact values as hard tokens. The compact sequence reduces later-layer computation and yields reusable KV caches.
a4j6KMRWSL.key_idea: Use the GDN delta update's recurrent signal to decide which context is already absorbed, merge it into soft tokens, and protect exact values as hard tokens.
a4j6KMRWSL.evidence: Experiments on long-horizon agent tasks against the uncompressed agent and trained compressors; reviews cite OfficeBench, AppWorld, and 8-Objective QA, attention-pair accounting, component ablations, and a cache-reuse experiment.
a4j6KMRWSL.claimed_gains: ASTC matches or exceeds the uncompressed agent's accuracy with up to 59.84% fewer end-to-end Attention Pairs, while trained compressors require 12.3x--194.9x more Attention Pairs per successful task.
a4j6KMRWSL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find that using the model's own recurrent signals to choose what to compress, without training a compressor and with exact values kept, is a simple and coherent idea backed by useful ablation and cache-reuse controls.
a4j6KMRWSL.main_concern: Reviewers say the headline claims exceed the results: the largest saving comes from one benchmark where accuracy is below the base agent, accuracy gains are tiny, and comparisons lack latency measurements and baselines such as FastKV and KVzip.

i9flfkn3pN.one_liner: Two distribution-matching distillation methods for continuous diffusion language models, using continuous token relaxation or categorical sampling, supporting multi-step generation.
i9flfkn3pN.problem: Continuous diffusion language models need many sequential network evaluations, and distributional distillation, which could exploit the discrete structure of language and enable multi-step generation, is underexplored in this setting.
i9flfkn3pN.method: The paper unifies existing distributional distillation approaches to show how the student's probabilistic parameterization determines the available gradient estimators. It then builds two methods sharing a student architecture and reverse-KL objective, Simplex-DMD (continuous token relaxation, pathwise gradients) and Reinforce-DMD (categorical token sampling, REINFORCE with a learned density ratio), both extended to multi-step generation.
i9flfkn3pN.key_idea: Distill with a reverse-KL objective where the student's token parameterization sets the estimator: pathwise gradients via simplex relaxation, or REINFORCE with a learned density ratio on sampled tokens.
i9flfkn3pN.evidence: Experiments on OpenWebText with sequence length 1,024, measuring the generative perplexity-entropy frontier against competing methods.
i9flfkn3pN.claimed_gains: At comparable entropy, Simplex-DMD reduces generative perplexity by 49% at 4 network evaluations, while Reinforce-DMD achieves a 20% reduction at 256 (the abstract is cut off after this).
i9flfkn3pN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified formulation clarifies relationships among distribution-matching distillation techniques and that Simplex-DMD shows a clear advantage on the generative perplexity-entropy frontier in few-step sampling.
i9flfkn3pN.main_concern: Reviewers say both methods are slight modifications of standard DMD and that the evidence rests on single-seed OpenWebText runs judged mainly by generative perplexity and unigram entropy.

ac6BotAkVF.one_liner: Critic-free policy optimization that measures turn-level credit by replaying environment states with a localized action change.
ac6BotAkVF.problem: Multi-turn agent training with sparse episode rewards makes it hard to tell which actions contributed to the outcome, and standard credit methods infer credit from trajectory statistics or rely on compute-heavy rollout sampling.
ac6BotAkVF.method: RMPO restores the execution state in the environment, applies a localized change to an action, and evaluates the outcome difference through a common replay interface, adding normalized replay measurements to the episode-level advantage. It offers three credit operators: leave-one-out action deletion, prefix-progress scoring, and same-state action replacement.
ac6BotAkVF.key_idea: Measure each turn's credit directly by resetting the environment, changing one action, and comparing outcomes, then add the normalized difference to the episode-level advantage.
ac6BotAkVF.evidence: Evaluation in ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B against GRPO and GiGPO, with analyses of replay coverage, execution cost, and partial ablations.
ac6BotAkVF.claimed_gains: RMPO consistently outperforms GRPO and GiGPO, deletion measurements correlate with symbolic-planner progress in ALFWorld (rho=0.842), and RMPO exceeds four-continuation sampling at equal GPU-hours (90.5% versus 85.5%).
ac6BotAkVF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the replay-based credit construction is simple, clearly explained, and broadly applicable to agentic LLM training, with replay needed only at training time.
ac6BotAkVF.main_concern: Reviewers worry that replay credit is biased shaping that may undervalue information-gathering actions and discourage exploration, that novelty over leave-one-out and counterfactual credit is limited, and that a resettable environment is required.

WXHd3txBCz.one_liner: Online RL jointly learning thinking-versus-direct routing and mode-conditioned responses via paired counterfactual rollouts and routing-token credit.
WXHd3txBCz.problem: Reasoning models often produce long chains of thought when direct answers suffice, and automating mode selection is hard because routing targets evolve with the policy, strong initial mode preferences destabilize exploration, and sequence-level objectives entangle routing with response learning.
WXHd3txBCz.method: CounterRoute trains one shared policy from a native dual-mode checkpoint without method-specific SFT warm-up. Paired current-policy counterfactual rollouts estimate cross-mode routing credit assigned only to the routing token, within-mode GRPO trains response tokens, and a paired-to-self-routed curriculum forces coverage of both modes before moving to autonomous routing.
WXHd3txBCz.key_idea: Assign cross-mode counterfactual credit from paired rollouts only to the routing token while within-mode GRPO trains response tokens, with a curriculum from forced pairing to self-routing.
WXHd3txBCz.evidence: Nine benchmarks at two Qwen3 scales against heuristic and learned adaptive-routing methods, with ablations and evaluation on domains unseen during RL training.
WXHd3txBCz.claimed_gains: CounterRoute improves macro-average accuracy at both Qwen3 scales while cutting mean generated tokens by 51% and 41%, respectively, versus always-thinking checkpoints.
WXHd3txBCz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical, the separation of routing credit from response credit is clean, and evaluation on nine benchmarks at two model scales shows clear token savings.
WXHd3txBCz.main_concern: Accuracy gains over Think-Only are narrow and largely driven by IFBench, prompt-level routing is not clearly shown, and novelty over Thinkless and HGPO is questioned.

6wfS5dCSF7.one_liner: Linear probe over frozen LLM layer-head attention profiles that scores candidate sentences for citation in one generation pass.
6wfS5dCSF7.problem: Sentence-level citation for RAG faces a trade-off: perturbation-based methods need repeated LLM inference, while attention-based methods use fixed aggregation rules that obscure informative variation across layers and heads.
6wfS5dCSF7.method: For each candidate sentence, CiteProbe builds an attention profile of the attention it receives from response tokens across individual layers and heads, and a lightweight model-specific linear probe maps these profiles to citation scores. All candidate sentences are scored from a single generation pass.
6wfS5dCSF7.key_idea: Treat citation as a readout problem: preserve the full layer-head attention profile of each candidate sentence and learn a linear probe from it to citation scores.
6wfS5dCSF7.evidence: Experiments across six LLMs and four datasets; reviews also cite held-out-dataset evaluation, surrogate experiments, and a cost comparison with ARC-JSD.
6wfS5dCSF7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical, reuses generation computation at low extra inference cost, and is backed by thorough experiments and analyses.
6wfS5dCSF7.main_concern: Reviewers say the closest prior method, AT2, which also learns per-head attention coefficients, is neither cited nor evaluated, so the novelty of learning a readout is overstated.

vGqhl0qIm5.one_liner: Single-loop, Hessian-free federated bilevel algorithm for client-specific lower-level inequality constraints via a gap function reformulation.
vGqhl0qIm5.problem: Existing federated bilevel methods assume unconstrained lower-level problems, which excludes applications with fairness constraints, resource budgets, or safety requirements.
vGqhl0qIm5.method: FedBiC handles a convex lower-level objective with general client-specific convex inequality constraints using a gap function reformulation. It is single-loop and Hessian-free, supports partial client participation, and requires no bound on client heterogeneity.
vGqhl0qIm5.key_idea: Reformulate the constrained lower level through a gap function, so a penalized single-loop Hessian-free federated method can handle client-specific inequality constraints.
vGqhl0qIm5.evidence: Convergence theory under partial and full client participation, and experiments on federated constrained LASSO, fair few-shot meta-learning, and federated steering.
vGqhl0qIm5.claimed_gains: FedBiC attains an O(1/sqrt(pK)) rate to a stationary point of the penalized objective under fixed penalty and partial participation, and with increasing penalty and full participation an O(1/K^((1-2rho)/2)) stationarity rate with an O(K^(-rho)) rate on the clientwise lower-level gap violation.
vGqhl0qIm5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree this is the first federated bilevel method with general client-specific lower-level inequality constraints, with a convergence analysis that handles partial participation and stale client states.
vGqhl0qIm5.main_concern: Guarantees under partial participation cover only stationarity of the fixed-penalty objective, stronger results need full participation and extra assumptions, and experimental baselines differ in several factors at once.

NyTAMmhp39.one_liner: Training-free caching for diffusion world models that reuses stable singular subspaces and linearly extrapolates singular values across denoising steps.
NyTAMmhp39.problem: Diffusion-based world models have substantial inference overhead from repeated Transformer evaluations during denoising, and existing caching exploits only feature- or token-level temporal redundancy.
NyTAMmhp39.method: SpectralCache reuses stable singular subspaces of features across nearby denoising steps and estimates only the low-dimensional singular values by linear extrapolation. It also skips selected backbone evaluations via singular value scaling, using spectral consistency between neighboring full-computation features.
NyTAMmhp39.key_idea: Cache the singular subspaces of intermediate features, which stay stable across denoising steps, and predict only the singular values by linear extrapolation.
NyTAMmhp39.evidence: Experiments on representative world models, including HunyuanWorld-Voyager-13B and Aether-5B per reviews, reporting WorldScore and 3D reconstruction metrics.
NyTAMmhp39.claimed_gains: On HunyuanWorld-Voyager-13B, SpectralCache achieves 5.22x acceleration while maintaining a WorldScore of 65.90 for static scenes.
NyTAMmhp39.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free, and timely, with better speedup and quality than prior caching methods at negligible overhead.
NyTAMmhp39.main_concern: Reviewers cite no theoretical justification for the stable subspaces and linear singular-value evolution, limited ablation of key components, and a quality drop from singular value scaling (PSNR 26.09 to 25.06).

q50ElljMQ8.one_liner: Reliability wrapper that trains iterative neural operators toward physically valid fixed points and physics-qualifies accelerated updates at inference.
q50ElljMQ8.problem: Iterative neural operators can reach a learned fixed point that remains physically invalid, and fast fixed-point acceleration can worsen this failure under distribution shift.
q50ElljMQ8.method: PHYSSAFE-IRNO applies stationarity-conditioned physical-risk supervision and averagedness-oriented regularization during training. At inference, a physics-qualified SuperMann solver screens fast proposals with a learned-physical bi-residual filter and falls back to separating-halfspace or Krasnosel'skii-Mann updates.
q50ElljMQ8.key_idea: Penalize physical violations near learned stationary points in training, then accept accelerated fixed-point proposals at inference only if a learned-plus-physical bi-residual filter admits them.
q50ElljMQ8.evidence: Convergence theory under an exactly averaged refinement map and a calibrated residual-envelope condition, plus experiments across four PDE systems and six held-out shifts with a disjoint physical audit.
q50ElljMQ8.claimed_gains: Across four PDE systems and six held-out shifts, aggregate error falls from 0.087 for physics-aware Anderson acceleration and 0.092 for a second baseline (the new value is cut off in the abstract).
q50ElljMQ8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between numerical stationarity and physical validity is well motivated, the physics-risk loss targets violations near learned fixed points, and empirical gains over baselines are clear.
q50ElljMQ8.main_concern: Theorem 1 assumes an exactly averaged refinement map, but the implementation only encourages averagedness, so the convergence guarantee may not apply to trained models.

FJqWrKoKKW.one_liner: Probes multimodal models with controlled candidate-answer sets, locating an answer bottleneck, and exploits it with two-stage answer selection.
FJqWrKoKKW.problem: Multimodal language models can encode useful visual information and still answer incorrectly, and it is unclear whether the failure lies in encoding or in determining the answer.
FJqWrKoKKW.method: The study varies a Guided Answer Space (GAS), an explicit set of candidate answers, while holding image, question, and target answer fixed, and intervenes on intermediate representations. It then builds a two-stage inference procedure that constructs a GAS from other models' answers and selects the final answer from it, without ground-truth access.
FJqWrKoKKW.key_idea: Vary the candidate-answer set (Guided Answer Space) with image, question, and target fixed, and intervene on intermediate visual states to locate where answers depend on visual tokens.
FJqWrKoKKW.evidence: Eleven models on TextVQA and GQA with controlled interventions (corruption transfer, freezing intermediate states, harder-distractor controls), plus a two-stage inference experiment using other models' answers.
FJqWrKoKKW.claimed_gains: Two-choice selection depends on visual tokens through fewer layers than open-ended answering, with a median difference equivalent to 42% of model depth, and the two-stage procedure with one answer from each of two other models corrects a third of the target model's open-ended errors and improves accuracy by 2.49 percentage points.
FJqWrKoKKW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper usefully separates visual encoding from answer determination, with a broad, carefully controlled investigation whose depth ordering holds across all eleven models on both datasets.
FJqWrKoKKW.main_concern: Reviewers say the interventions do not show that the needed information was available for originally misanswered examples, and the two-stage procedure is a modest generate-then-select method lacking budget-matched ensemble baselines.

UYnfig3045.one_liner: Jointly trains an LLM as privileged self-teacher and student, KL-regularizing the teacher toward the student for on-policy distillation.
UYnfig3045.problem: Privileged information can let a self-distillation teacher solve tasks through shortcuts unavailable to the student, so even a higher-performing teacher can give guidance that degrades student performance.
UYnfig3045.method: The paper derives a necessary and sufficient condition for the teacher's local distillation update to be a positive multiple of the student's reward gradient, and turns it into a teacher-training surrogate that jointly optimizes teacher and student with KL regularization and dense on-policy distillation. Reviews name the variants JOLT and JOLT+ (JOLT with student rewards).
UYnfig3045.key_idea: Train the privileged teacher so its distillation update aligns with the student's reward gradient, using KL regularization to keep teacher guidance matched to the student's current behavior.
UYnfig3045.evidence: A derived necessary and sufficient condition for update alignment, plus experiments that reviews describe as covering MATH, GSM8K, coding (LCBv6), AppWorld, and Terminal-Bench with several Qwen3 and DeepSeek-V2-Lite models.
UYnfig3045.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between a teacher that solves tasks and one that gives supervision suited to the current student is useful, and that training the teacher toward the student is coherent and novel.
UYnfig3045.main_concern: Reviewers say the empirical evidence is uneven, with models and benchmarks varying by setting, an LCBv6 gain that is not evidence of generalization, JOLT falling below GRPO in agentic settings without student rewards, and theory that does not cover the implemented joint update.

4a4cItaNf8.one_liner: Defines occupancy Rashomon capacity and proves an Omega(M/b) state-query lower bound for auditing families of near-optimal RL policies.
4a4cItaNf8.problem: Near-optimal reinforcement-learning policies can have different reachable behavior, but their number alone does not determine how difficult they are to audit.
4a4cItaNf8.method: The paper defines occupancy Rashomon capacity as the metric entropy of near-optimal discounted state-action occupancies within a declared deployment class, and proves that a separated family of M policies with b-sparse exact local signatures needs Omega(M/b) state queries for occupancy identification. It adds a hidden-branch MDP attaining the bound, a shortest-path family with efficient audits, a root-reset episode law, and a noisy-trigger lower bound.
4a4cItaNf8.key_idea: Audit difficulty is set by how much each local query reveals about the policy family (b-sparse signatures), not by the family's size or capacity alone.
4a4cItaNf8.evidence: Lower-bound theory with hidden-branch MDP and shortest-path constructions, plus learned SAC policy families on AntMaze with 20,000 independent trajectories per checkpoint.
4a4cItaNf8.claimed_gains: A separated family of M policies with b-sparse exact local signatures requires Omega(M/b) state queries, and a simultaneous certificate over 50 checkpoints finds a 23-member separated packing among 30 pipeline-relative near-optimal policies.
4a4cItaNf8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the message that policy multiplicity is not the same as auditing difficulty is clean and useful, with the hidden-branch versus shortest-path contrast making it concrete and the assumptions carefully stated.
4a4cItaNf8.main_concern: Reviewers say the main bound is a classical hidden-index search argument that the authors acknowledge, so the contribution is mostly definitions and framing, and the theory is disconnected from the AntMaze experiments.

XlIKYY6PqM.one_liner: Ranks unlabeled images by reconstruction code length of a corruption-reconstruction network and keeps the worst-compressed half for pretraining.
XlIKYY6PqM.problem: Selecting training data typically requires labels, captions, or an externally pretrained encoder, which an unlabeled image pool lacks, and what makes an image useful for self-supervised pretraining is unsettled.
XlIKYY6PqM.method: A corruption-reconstruction network is trained on the pool, and its per-image loss is read as a conditional code length (nats to encode the image given a masked and noised view). Images are ranked by this CORE score and those the model compresses worst are kept.
XlIKYY6PqM.key_idea: Score each image by the per-image reconstruction loss of a model trained on the pool, read as conditional code length, and keep the images that compress worst.
XlIKYY6PqM.evidence: ImageNet-1k MAE pretraining with linear probing and ADE20K mIoU, five pixel-prediction backbones plus DINO, a held-out scorer experiment, and selection from ImageNet-21k.
XlIKYY6PqM.claimed_gains: On ImageNet-1k, MAE on the top-scored 50% at half the gradient steps reaches 62.1% linear probing versus 62.3% for the full set (random 50%: 56.7%), and at equal steps the top half exceeds the full set by 5.9 linear-probe points and 1.1 ADE20K mIoU.
XlIKYY6PqM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the selection signal is consistent and well controlled, with the top > random > bottom ordering holding across five pixel-prediction backbones and DINO, held-out scoring, and transfer to other datasets.
XlIKYY6PqM.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited and closest prior work is missing, since the rule resembles perplexity-based data pruning and the code-length framing does not explain downstream value, and the large equal-step gains lack a total-budget baseline.

OpkwzHQVHQ.one_liner: Feynman-Kac analysis gives closed-form bias of diffusion posterior sampling and explains discretization instability, motivating implicit guidance updates.
OpkwzHQVHQ.problem: Diffusion-based posterior samplers are biased even with exact prior scores, and in hard-constraint regimes such as low measurement noise the discretized DPS algorithm is numerically unstable.
OpkwzHQVHQ.method: The paper introduces a surrogate curve of densities interpolating between the true posterior and the standard Gaussian, whose density ratio with the sampler solves a parabolic PDE with a Feynman-Kac representation. It also shows that DPS instability motivates implicit (backward-Euler) guidance updates and characterizes the secondary bias of early guidance-stopping.
OpkwzHQVHQ.key_idea: Write the DPS-to-surrogate density ratio as a Feynman-Kac path expectation to expose sampling bias, and trace instability to guidance strength scaling inversely with step size.
OpkwzHQVHQ.evidence: Mathematical derivations, including Theorems 1 and 2 per reviews; the visible abstract does not describe experiments.
OpkwzHQVHQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the closed-form quantification of DPS bias useful and novel, since it shows which posterior regions are over- or under-sampled and points to designs with smaller bias.
OpkwzHQVHQ.main_concern: Reviewers raise technical gaps: Theorem 2 needs smoothness that the reward -||A(x)-y|| lacks, the analysis may not hold for low-dimensional manifold data, and no concrete method improvement is proposed.

HU33BX9cUe.one_liner: Prospective study of memory policies (retain, discount, reset, multiscale LETHE) for personalized reward models, separating change detection from adaptation.
HU33BX9cUe.problem: Temporal personalization often assumes that once preference change is detected the model should adapt its use of history, which collapses three questions: whether there is enough evidence for this user, how memory should change, and whether adaptation is driven by that user.
HU33BX9cUe.method: The study fixes a pairwise personalized reward model with one component learned across training users and varies only how the user-memory component builds a user's history, comparing retain, discount, reset, and a multiscale LETHE mode that learns a mixture of causal memories at different timescales. Evaluation is prospective, using only information available before evaluation.
HU33BX9cUe.key_idea: Hold the reward model fixed and vary only the user-memory rule, evaluating prospectively, to test whether detected population change is individually actionable.
HU33BX9cUe.evidence: Controlled synthetic histories and the PENS, PRISM, and Chatbot Arena datasets, with predict-before-update evaluation and shared-alarm comparisons.
HU33BX9cUe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating change detection from memory adaptation is a meaningful framing and that the prospective protocol, shared-alarm comparisons, and transparent negative findings give useful controls.
HU33BX9cUe.main_concern: Reviewers say the strongest findings come from synthetic histories and a fixed linear predictor while natural PRISM and Arena results are mostly inconclusive, so the link to real personalized reward models is limited.

4JKZDLeJC2.one_liner: Discrete flow matching over a four-move arrow alphabet that conserves electrons exactly and yields chemist-readable reaction mechanisms.
4JKZDLeJC2.problem: Generative reaction models that edit one entry of a bond-electron matrix at a time conserve the electron count exactly only if deterministic in every entry, so validity and conservation otherwise need filtering or resampling.
4JKZDLeJC2.method: Arrow Flow Matching (AFM) represents the state as an integer bond-electron matrix and trains a Markov chain by discrete flow matching whose elementary event is one move from a four-element alphabet, the matrix form of a chemist's arrow. Every move preserves the electron count, and the chain may stop only where a table of valid per-atom states allows.
4JKZDLeJC2.key_idea: Make the elementary event of the Markov chain an electron-pair arrow move rather than an entry edit, so conservation is an algebraic identity and validity a table lookup.
4JKZDLeJC2.evidence: A proof about entrywise independent models, and accuracy comparisons against earlier retrained models and an entrywise model, including model sizes, distribution shifts, and an expert-arrow agreement table per reviews.
4JKZDLeJC2.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says the guarantees cost almost no accuracy and that AFM and the entrywise model are more accurate than every earlier model retrained.
4JKZDLeJC2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that enforcing electron conservation through the elementary event is a clean structural principle, with validity and conservation guaranteed at little accuracy cost and a clear presentation.
4JKZDLeJC2.main_concern: Reviewers say the necessity of AFM is not established because no filtering-and-resampling baseline for Discrete FlowER is measured, and the arrow-interpretability result lacks a control using the paper's own decomposition.

bQqcOEDj7K.one_liner: Gap-free analysis of Oja's streaming PCA under general stochastic updates, with a near-matching lower bound and private PCA application.
bQqcOEDj7K.problem: Near-optimal streaming PCA rates previously required eigengap assumptions or rank-one updates, so the gap-free setting with general stochastic updates lacked a near-optimal analysis.
bQqcOEDj7K.method: The paper analyzes Oja's algorithm using only a second-moment bound on individual stochastic updates rather than almost-sure bounds, and proves a nearly matching lower bound. It extends the result to a Rayleigh-quotient notion of approximate PCA and applies it to gap-free differentially private PCA for sub-Gaussian data.
bQqcOEDj7K.key_idea: A trace and weak-majorization bound on products of stochastic update matrices needs only second-moment control of updates, bypassing almost-sure norm bounds and matrix Bernstein.
bQqcOEDj7K.evidence: Theoretical guarantees (Theorem 1, lower bound Theorem 4, private PCA Theorem 3) plus experiments on Gaussian data with grid-searched step sizes, including private settings with d=5000 and n up to 10^8 per reviews.
bQqcOEDj7K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree Theorem 1 is a substantive generalization of streaming-PCA theory (gap-free, unrestricted rank, second-moment assumption) with a nontrivial proof and lower bounds that support the parameter dependence.
bQqcOEDj7K.main_concern: The private result assumes a publicly known lambda_1 (and nu), so the claim of settling Brown's conjecture is overstated, and the experiments are narrow (Gaussian data) with unclear computational cost for the full-batch private algorithm.

IAmkHtbnXd.one_liner: Groups users with similar practices into separate persona skills, generates answers per skill, and merges them to resolve conflicts.
IAmkHtbnXd.problem: Persona skills distilled from multiple users' work records can contain incompatible recommendations for the same situation, and existing methods do not preserve or coordinate these conflicts.
IAmkHtbnXd.method: ConCord extracts context-dependent decision rules per user, groups users with similar practices, and builds one skill per group so conflicting approaches stay separate. For each task, separate agents answer with different skills and a merging LLM resolves conflicts based on the task requirements.
IAmkHtbnXd.key_idea: Cluster users by practice, keep conflicting practices in separate skills, and merge per-skill drafts with an LLM that resolves conflicts per task.
IAmkHtbnXd.evidence: Four datasets of user work records covering workplace communication, software issue handling, and computer-science question answering, with four base models, five baselines, and a Claude Haiku 4.5 judge.
IAmkHtbnXd.claimed_gains: An average score improvement of 0.34 over responses generated without skills, compared with 0.14 for the strongest baseline.
IAmkHtbnXd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conflicting user practices are a useful problem, that keeping them in separate skills is a meaningful approach, and that evaluation spans several datasets, base models, and conflict-handling alternatives.
IAmkHtbnXd.main_concern: Gains are confounded with extra computation (four calls and 7,400 tokens versus one call and 1,444 tokens), with no equal-budget baseline, and quality is judged only by one LLM without human validation.

FX2vBjYfZN.one_liner: BYON adds image-adaptive latent noise from token saliency and a reconstruction-reliability gate on latent prediction in masked image modeling.
FX2vBjYfZN.problem: Combining reconstruction and latent prediction is not additive: Gaussian latent noise adds nothing to masked image modeling, and a bootstrapped latent-prediction loss lowers accuracy.
FX2vBjYfZN.method: Image-adaptive noise sets each image's noise level from its token saliency, and a reliability gate scales the latent-prediction loss by the current reconstruction error.
FX2vBjYfZN.key_idea: Set per-image latent noise level from token saliency and scale the latent-prediction loss by the current reconstruction error, so alignment targets are trusted only when reliable.
FX2vBjYfZN.evidence: A ViT-B pretrained for 400 epochs on ImageNet-1K with matched epochs, data, code base and hardware, evaluated by fine-tuning, linear probe, ADE20K and detection, with factorial ablations and some five-seed results (per reviews).
FX2vBjYfZN.claimed_gains: The gate alone returns accuracy to 82.84%, adaptive noise alone reaches 83.16% and both reach 83.56%; BYON improves over masked and denoising pre-training by 0.7 points on ImageNet-1K fine-tuning, 2.2 under a linear probe, 1.4 mIoU on ADE20K and 1.7 box AP.
FX2vBjYfZN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question meaningful, the factorial ablation of noise and gate informative, and the gains consistent across downstream tasks with the added training cost reported.
FX2vBjYfZN.main_concern: It is not isolated whether gains come from matching noise to image content rather than from a better noise-level distribution, and the matched-budget comparison hides about 40% more FLOPs than DiffMAE.

RCfvUZ2kP8.one_liner: Diagnostic using morally unambiguous value-conflict scenarios to measure alignment faking in LLMs, with label-free steering mitigation.
RCfvUZ2kP8.problem: Prior alignment-faking diagnostics use highly harmful scenarios that make most models refuse immediately, so models never deliberate over policy, monitoring, or consequences.
