bTZVvwj6R6.evidence: Controlled empirical studies of action chunking, overfitting, and Markovianized data across manipulation tasks.
bTZVvwj6R6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the fast, controllable GPU-accelerated infrastructure and its utility for isolating behavioral cloning phenomena like action chunking.
bTZVvwj6R6.main_concern: Reviewers criticize that the "human-like" premise is assumed and qualitatively argued rather than quantitatively validated against real human trajectories, and that scripted policy details are underspecified.

NPhDWygvtu.one_liner: Allocates discrete latent cell widths by decoder sensitivity so an autoregressive prior generates manifold samples in one decoder pass.
NPhDWygvtu.problem: Uniform latent quantization induces uneven geodesic distortion on Riemannian manifolds, while trajectory-based manifold samplers are slow.
NPhDWygvtu.method: RiCoTA partitions latent coordinates by average decoder sensitivity to equalize intrinsic distortion at a fixed cell count, trains with uniform within-cell reconstruction, and samples via an autoregressive cell prior plus one decoder evaluation.
NPhDWygvtu.key_idea: Adapts per-coordinate latent quantization cell widths to inverse decoder sensitivity so an autoregressive discrete prior + uniform cell sample yields one-step manifold generation.
NPhDWygvtu.evidence: Supported by asymptotic distortion and population error bounds, held-out sensitivity diagnostics, and experiments across manifold benchmarks and DNA.
NPhDWygvtu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the sensitivity-based companding motivation conceptually appealing and supported by mathematical analysis and comprehensive benchmarks.
NPhDWygvtu.main_concern: Reviewers note missing standard deviations across seeds in main tables, unclear scalability to high-dimensional manifolds without DNA-specific modifications, and dense, hard-to-follow writing.

EbrsANKCOn.one_liner: Uniformly replays one verified example per discovered solution mode to prevent mode collapse in RLVR post-training.
EbrsANKCOn.problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards concentrates probability onto fewer correct solution modes even as overall accuracy holds or improves.
EbrsANKCOn.method: The authors introduce ModeBench to measure mode discovery and propose Re:Max, which stores one verified example per discovered mode in a replay buffer and trains on stored modes uniformly.
EbrsANKCOn.key_idea: Store one verified example per discovered solution mode in a replay buffer and sample them uniformly during RLVR training.
EbrsANKCOn.evidence: Experiments evaluate ModeBench across three model scales, two RL objectives, and harder task constructions.
EbrsANKCOn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper studies an important diversity-collapse problem and that ModeBench and PCMD provide useful, reproducible ways to measure mode diversity.
EbrsANKCOn.main_concern: Reviewers note that Re:Max requires explicit mode labels that standard RLVR verifiers lack, and that evidence is limited to small models and synthetic tasks.

iT4iXqvAA0.one_liner: Evaluates coding agents on 200 repository tasks interleaved with other unfinished tasks in matched uninterrupted vs. switched sessions.
iT4iXqvAA0.problem: Standard repository coding benchmarks test one issue at a time, overlooking whether agents retain focus after working on other unfinished tasks.
iT4iXqvAA0.method: Switch-SWE reconstructs 200 focus tasks from 19 Python repositories into 400 matched uninterrupted and switched sessions with persistent checkouts and executable verifiers, measuring focus-task resolution drops from interleaved task stages.
iT4iXqvAA0.key_idea: Compares coding agents in paired uninterrupted versus task-interleaved repository sessions with identical focus requirements and executable verifiers.
iT4iXqvAA0.evidence: Evaluated 7 coding agents across 200 Switch-SWE focus tasks from 19 Python repositories plus trajectory error analysis.
iT4iXqvAA0.claimed_gains: Interleaved unfinished work causes an average focus-task resolution drop of 11.5 percentage points (ranging from 6.0 to 15.0 points) across 7 coding agents.
iT4iXqvAA0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practically relevant task-resumption problem and the carefully controlled paired-session protocol across 200 executable tasks.
iT4iXqvAA0.main_concern: Reviewers note that switched sessions confound resumption with longer context/history and potential timeout-budget consumption, while the proposed RCM mitigation is only lightly evaluated.

pzz5kZtrOR.one_liner: Characterizes exact geometric conditions under which the SPO+ surrogate identifies the conditional mean cost vector modulo decision-invisible directions.
pzz5kZtrOR.problem: Decision-focused surrogates like SPO+ can yield optimal downstream decisions without uniquely identifying the underlying predictive cost report.
pzz5kZtrOR.method: The authors quotient out directions orthogonal to the feasible set's affine span and characterize the population-risk equality set of SPO+. Under central symmetry (and via reflected crossing without symmetry), unique quotient-report identification holds iff every nonzero displacement crosses an optimal face with positive probability.
pzz5kZtrOR.key_idea: Quotients out decision-invisible directions to establish that SPO+ uniquely identifies the conditional mean report iff nonzero displacements cross shifted optimal faces with positive probability.
pzz5kZtrOR.evidence: Supported by population identification theorems, polytope quadratic-growth bounds, and empirical studies on Portfolio, KuaiRec, Energy/Storage, and synthetic DGP companions.
pzz5kZtrOR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the quotient-space formulation separating decision optimality from report identification and the rigorous handling of ties on optimal faces.
pzz5kZtrOR.main_concern: Reviewers find the presentation hard to follow and note limited incremental novelty over Liu & Grigas (2021)'s known SPO+ excess-risk identity.

sbgflATGFK.one_liner: Routes causally attributed multimodal agent experiences between external memory and model weights based on transferability and stability.
sbgflATGFK.problem: Multimodal agents must decide which experiences belong in reversible external memory versus consolidated parametric weights without internalizing spurious behaviors.
sbgflATGFK.method: VisEvolver extracts causal experience via visual counterfactual attribution and routes validated items along an Experience-Evidence-Skill-Program-Weight lifecycle using cross-task support, stability, specificity, and conflict signals.
sbgflATGFK.key_idea: Filters multimodal experience via visual counterfactual attribution and routes items between external memory and weight updates by transferability and stability.
sbgflATGFK.evidence: Evaluations on ChartQA, InfographicVQA, VisualToolBench, and EB-ALFRED with Qwen3.5-9B, plus synthetic router analyses.
sbgflATGFK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit framing of routing experiences between external memory and model weights.
sbgflATGFK.main_concern: Evidence rests on small, screened challenge subsets with single deterministic runs and tiny margins over single-branch baselines, without variance or significance tests.

nVAjpjQ5y1.one_liner: Allocates mixed-precision quantization bit-widths in multimodal MoE models using hierarchical Owen attribution and within-expert Harsanyi interactions.
nVAjpjQ5y1.problem: Scalar expert-importance scores for MoE mixed-precision quantization ignore cross-expert context dependence, expert-projection hierarchy, and coupled within-expert quantization effects.
nVAjpjQ5y1.method: Config-Owen formulates expert precision allocation as a cooperative game, computing configuration-valued utilities via Owen-style hierarchical attribution and within-expert Harsanyi interactions across projection triplets. It then solves a multiple-choice knapsack problem (MCKP) under a global memory budget.
nVAjpjQ5y1.key_idea: Estimates configuration-valued expert utilities using hierarchical Owen attribution and Harsanyi interactions, then solves an exact MCKP for mixed-precision bit-width assignment.
nVAjpjQ5y1.evidence: Evaluated across four multimodal MoE models and Mixtral-8x7B with component ablations (Table 7) against Uniform, Hessian, and PMQ baselines.
nVAjpjQ5y1.claimed_gains: On DeepSeek-VL2-S at 2.58 bits, Config-Owen retains 98.39% of the FP16 five-task average score.
nVAjpjQ5y1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling joint within-expert projection configurations rather than independent scalar scores is well-motivated and supported by ablations.
nVAjpjQ5y1.main_concern: Reviewers note that additive MCKP allocation and restricted all-high/baseline contexts overlook cross-expert interactions, while game-theoretic bounds are disconnected from the algorithm.

qlo2ebi6wq.one_liner: Benchmarks one-shot LLM-generated code for adapting scientific lossy compressors to preserve 83 derived features.
qlo2ebi6wq.problem: Pointwise error-bounded lossy compressors distort derived scientific quantities like spectra and topology, while manual feature-preserving designs do not generalize across features.
qlo2ebi6wq.method: CraftBench evaluates LLM-generated compressor adaptations across 83 feature-preservation tasks under three modes—error bounding, configuration selection, and error correction—requiring solutions to reduce feature distortion while beating a uniform-tightening storage baseline.
qlo2ebi6wq.key_idea: Tests whether LLM-generated compressor adaptations preserve executable scientific features better than uniformly tightening the global error bound.
qlo2ebi6wq.evidence: Evaluated across 83 feature-preservation tasks on scientific fields using compressors including ZFP and SZ3.
qlo2ebi6wq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the uniform-tightening baseline and joint evaluation of feature preservation and total storage cost.
qlo2ebi6wq.main_concern: Reviewers note narrow data diversity (74 of 83 tasks share one temperature field), single-shot generation without feedback, and fixed configurations outperforming adaptive LLM selection.

xtFb3hkqB2.one_liner: Restores LLM output diversity via candidate-selection probability calibration followed by Pareto-filtered guided self-distillation.
xtFb3hkqB2.problem: LLMs concentrate probability mass on a few canonical responses, limiting output diversity across repeated samples without persistent prompting.
xtFb3hkqB2.method: CADI first calibrates length-normalized candidate-selection likelihoods to flatten excessive concentration while preserving preference order. It then performs online guided self-distillation, distilling guidance-conditioned responses only when they Pareto-improve over unguided outputs.
xtFb3hkqB2.key_idea: Combines length-normalized candidate-selection diversity calibration with Pareto-gated online distillation from guided generations.
xtFb3hkqB2.evidence: Evaluated on NoveltyBench and Artificial Hivemind across two open-weight LLM backbones (plus 32B/70B and GSM8K appendix checks).
xtFb3hkqB2.claimed_gains: Outperforms training-based baselines in semantic diversity and utility while largely preserving response quality (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
xtFb3hkqB2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree Stage 1 calibration is simple and produces consistent semantic diversity and utility gains across backbones.
xtFb3hkqB2.main_concern: Reviewers note Stage 2 adds little over Stage 1 despite high extra cost, and missing decoding-parameter sweeps leave open whether CADI beats tuned sampling at matched quality.

XJODsZUduW.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM and agentic judges on long computer-use trajectories using paired positive and instruction-swapped negative tasks.
XJODsZUduW.problem: Automated judges for long-horizon computer-use agents can be fooled by trajectories that appear complete but violate instruction constraints or cause side effects.
XJODsZUduW.method: The authors collect 1,373 computer-use tasks from 166 hours of human recordings across three OSes, construct hard negatives by swapping closely related instructions, and evaluate eleven judges across three splits.
XJODsZUduW.key_idea: Constructs paired positive-negative judge evaluation instances by recording closely related computer-use instructions and swapping their instructions.
XJODsZUduW.evidence: Evaluates eleven LLM and agentic judges on 1,373 tasks (with up to 300 screenshots) across AH, AH-S, and AH-D splits.
XJODsZUduW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the substantial annotation effort and the neat instruction-swapping design for testing long-horizon computer-use judges.
XJODsZUduW.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about missing code and dataset release for a benchmark paper, unclear outcome-vs-process evaluation objectives, and potential false negatives when swapping instructions.

eHXECvUB3O.one_liner: Benchmarks and models dynamic hierarchical rule interactions for multimodal content moderation using rule-relation graphs.
eHXECvUB3O.problem: Content moderation models are tuned for static rules and fail when hierarchical policies evolve, conflict, or face untrusted pseudo-rules in user content.
eHXECvUB3O.method: The authors build DynRule-Bench with controlled edits, source exchanges, and pseudo-rule insertions, and propose DynRule-Guard, which encodes a Rule Relation Graph into a latent state to compose Guidance Tokens from an Interaction Pattern Bank.
eHXECvUB3O.key_idea: Decomposes hierarchical moderation rules into a Rule Relation Graph and composes an Interaction Pattern Bank into a rule-interaction Guidance Token.
eHXECvUB3O.evidence: Evaluated on DynRule-Bench across Qwen, GLM, and InternVL backbones, plus external text evaluation on IHEval.
eHXECvUB3O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paired source-exchange protocol cleanly evaluates adaptation versus preservation under dynamic moderation rules.
eHXECvUB3O.main_concern: Reviewers point out irreconcilable dataset/metric counts in Table 15, in-distribution bias from training and testing on the same construction pipeline, and lack of external multimodal validation.

uvDmhHoVXw.one_liner: Designs commuting sum and ratio spectral graph filters for directed graphs using the spectral conjugate of the shift operator.
uvDmhHoVXw.problem: The skew-symmetric Cartesian split of a directed graph shift operator generally does not commute with the shift, breaking shift-invariance.
uvDmhHoVXw.method: The authors replace the Cartesian split with the spectral conjugate under complex conjugation of eigenvalues, splitting the shift into commuting dissipative and non-dissipative parts to define sum and ratio spectral graph filters.
uvDmhHoVXw.key_idea: Splits a directed graph shift operator via its commuting spectral conjugate to build non-holomorphic sum and ratio spectral filters.
uvDmhHoVXw.evidence: Theoretical long-range reach analysis on directed cycles plus graph transfer and node classification experiments.
uvDmhHoVXw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the commuting spectral conjugate operator construction an interesting theoretical approach to directed graph filtering.
uvDmhHoVXw.main_concern: Reviewers raise a correctness issue in the non-diagonalizable spectral conjugate definition dropping the nilpotent part, question non-normal norm preservation claims, and note missing recent baselines.

1D7AdV6IkB.one_liner: Combines learned latent dynamics, a VAE observation likelihood, and flow-matching ensemble filtering for sparse data assimilation.
1D7AdV6IkB.problem: High-dimensional nonlinear dynamics make repeated full-state forward simulation expensive, while sparse observations provide limited direct information for data assimilation.
1D7AdV6IkB.method: LD-EnFF performs sequential Bayesian filtering in a compact latent space using a learned latent dynamics surrogate (LDNet) for ensemble propagation and a VAE-based forward observation model to evaluate state-dependent likelihoods. At each step, an ensemble flow-matching update uses the forecast ensemble and latent likelihood to jointly update latent states and uncertain parameters.
1D7AdV6IkB.key_idea: Evaluates a state-dependent VAE observation likelihood in latent space and updates states and parameters via flow-matching ensemble filtering.
1D7AdV6IkB.evidence: Tested on Kolmogorov flow, tsunami propagation, and atmospheric modeling benchmarks against matched LDNet+LSTM and IEnKF baselines.
1D7AdV6IkB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning a forward latent-to-observation map to avoid full-state reconstruction is a sensible design for sparse data assimilation.
1D7AdV6IkB.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about missing simpler likelihood controls, limited generalization to time-dependent observation operators, and incomplete experimental comparisons.

e4gIZ5LcFm.one_liner: Enforces one-to-one patch assignment against a normal reference to trade off structural and logical anomaly sensitivity.
e4gIZ5LcFm.problem: Nearest-neighbor patch matching allows multiple test patches to match the same normal reference patch, hiding quantity and compositional changes in logical anomalies.
e4gIZ5LcFm.method: The authors replace nearest-neighbor patch matching with a one-to-one patch assignment between a test image and a normal reference while keeping features, patch costs, and aggregation fixed. They define assignment excess as the extra cost from one-to-one matching and use a calibrated form as an auxiliary signal in EfficientAD-M.
e4gIZ5LcFm.key_idea: Replaces independent nearest-neighbor patch matching with one-to-one patch assignment and quantifies its ranking effect via assignment excess.
e4gIZ5LcFm.evidence: Controlled experiments across encoders, reference constructions, and anomaly datasets, plus five training runs of EfficientAD-M.
e4gIZ5LcFm.claimed_gains: Improves logical anomaly detection in all five training runs when used in EfficientAD-M, with Appendix C.3 showing a 2.89-point gain over Chamfer on seed 0.
e4gIZ5LcFm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled comparison isolating the one-to-one matching constraint on an identical cost matrix is clean and insightful.
e4gIZ5LcFm.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty over prior optimal-transport/Hungarian anomaly detectors, missing baselines like ObjectCore/LogSAD/RAD, and single-seed baseline comparisons.

lEfFuKX6oA.one_liner: Uses an adaptive JEPA encoder and temporal predictor to learn stable cross-day representations from chronic neural recordings.
lEfFuKX6oA.problem: Recorded neural populations shift across days in chronic electrophysiology, hindering stable decoding and tracking of learning-related representational changes.
lEfFuKX6oA.method: NeuroLens builds on LeJEPA with an adaptive encoder using learnable queries and cross-attention to map varying neural populations into a shared latent space, paired with a temporal predictor forecasting future latent states. Pretrained across days, it supports decoding of decisions and sentence meaning while tracking cortical reorganization.
lEfFuKX6oA.key_idea: Maps changing neural populations into a shared latent space with an adaptive cross-attention encoder and forecasts future states via LeJEPA.
lEfFuKX6oA.evidence: Evaluated on mouse and human intracortical recordings and the FALCON benchmark against multiple neural decoding baselines.
lEfFuKX6oA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, addresses an important recording nonstationarity problem, and evaluates across multiple datasets and baselines.
lEfFuKX6oA.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient novelty discussion relative to prior neural JEPA/cross-attention works, missing cross-day baselines and statistical tests, and unverified separation of biological learning from nonstationarity.

gnGzF5LGOu.one_liner: Defines piecewise information limited (PIL) algorithms via max-information to formally bound and audit copyright memorization.
gnGzF5LGOu.problem: Existing copyright and privacy frameworks assume copyrighted works appear in isolated independent datapoints or require noisy differential privacy, failing under correlated data and noiseless mechanisms.
gnGzF5LGOu.method: The authors formalize piecewise information limited (PIL) algorithms, generalizing differential privacy to correlated datasets, noiseless mechanisms, and prompt-conditioned regurgitation risk. They also propose a memorization-testing auditing algorithm (ExtData) to verify compliance empirically.
gnGzF5LGOu.key_idea: Bounds correlated-data reconstruction and prompt-conditioned copyright regurgitation via max-information-based piecewise information limitation and memorization-testing audits.
gnGzF5LGOu.evidence: Formal theoretical framework relating PIL to differential privacy and memorization, plus empirical memorization tests (ExtData vs. MiniPrompt) on quotes and emails.
gnGzF5LGOu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the information-theoretic generalization beyond DP to correlated data and noiseless mechanisms, and the practical motivation for auditing regurgitation risk.
gnGzF5LGOu.main_concern: Reviewers note limited empirical validation (small quote/email sets without controlled canary-entropy audits), hard-to-compute theoretical quantities like conditional reconstruction entropy, and dense mathematical presentation.

J66QoSSPne.one_liner: Fine-tunes VLMs on a visual needle-in-a-haystack retrieval task to improve unseen multimodal many-shot classification scaling.
J66QoSSPne.problem: Vision-language models show inconsistent scaling on multimodal many-shot classification, and direct fine-tuning on many-shot classification fails to transfer to unseen tasks.
J66QoSSPne.method: The authors fine-tune VLMs for 200 gradient steps on a needle-in-a-haystack task where the target image and its label are hidden among context examples. Attention analyses show this objective reduces positional bias across the context, improving generalization to held-out many-shot classification tasks.
J66QoSSPne.key_idea: Replaces direct many-shot fine-tuning with 200 steps of visual needle-in-a-haystack retrieval SFT to flatten attention positional bias across long multimodal contexts.
J66QoSSPne.evidence: Evaluations across three VLM families on held-out many-shot classification datasets comparing NIH-SFT against matched-budget MS-SFT, plus attention entropy analyses.
J66QoSSPne.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the proxy needle-in-a-haystack training objective simple, counterintuitive, efficient (200 steps), and consistently effective across three model families.
J66QoSSPne.main_concern: Reviewers cite single-seed training on only three held-out datasets, no longer-budget MS-SFT control, missing image-shuffling controls to isolate visual use, and non-causal attention heuristics.

8qnklea4uX.one_liner: Tests how unverified compliance claims in agent reports reduce tool verification and increase false acceptance by LLM judges.
8qnklea4uX.problem: Tool-equipped LLM evaluators may skip verification and accept failing agent outputs when reports include unverified compliance claims.
8qnklea4uX.method: The authors hold the artifact, requirements, and verification tools fixed while varying a single report field (unverified claim, deleted, or measured value) across lens design, numerical integration, and prediction-market trading. They measure both tool-verification behavior and final acceptance under varying request limits and prompt instructions.
8qnklea4uX.key_idea: Isolates compliance-claim effects on LLM judges by varying a single report field while fixing artifacts, contracts, and verification tools, separately logging tool calls and verdicts.
8qnklea4uX.evidence: Controlled experiments across eight pooled LLM evaluators in three domains (lens design, numerical integration, prediction-market trading), request-limit sweeps, and a research-agent workflow.
8qnklea4uX.claimed_gains: Under a two-request limit, evaluators accepted failing lenses 44.5 percentage points more often with a compliance claim than a measured value (95% CI [27.0, 51.9]); in a later request-limit experiment the contrast was 37.0 points with two requests and 14.0 ([7.0, 17.9]) with five.
8qnklea4uX.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers praise the clean, controlled single-field intervention separating verification skipping from acceptance errors and the timely relevance to LLM-as-a-judge reward hacking.
8qnklea4uX.main_concern: Reviewers note the highly artificial, structured verification environments, unclear normative framing when prompts do not flag report fields as untrusted, and one reviewer flags severe writing clarity issues.

pEL9WvPxZo.one_liner: Wraps sequential data-acquisition policies with a calibration-based stopping selector that controls conditional risk on stopped samples.
pEL9WvPxZo.problem: Existing sequential acquisition and early-stopping heuristics lack finite-sample guarantees on decision risk among the samples where acquisition actually halts.
pEL9WvPxZo.method: Risk-Controlled Stopping (RCS) is a post-hoc, distribution-free wrapper that uses independent calibration trajectories to select a stopping rule controlling a user-specified conditional risk (such as FNR or FPR) among early-stopped samples. When no candidate rule can be certified, RCS defers to full acquisition without requiring policy retraining.
pEL9WvPxZo.key_idea: Applies calibration-based statistical testing over candidate stopping rules to certify conditional risk on early-stopped trajectories, deferring to full acquisition when infeasible.
pEL9WvPxZo.evidence: Finite-sample conditional risk guarantees and evaluations on synthetic CIFAR-10, FastMRI knee k-space acquisition, an internal prostate MRI cohort, and a learned RL acquisition policy.
pEL9WvPxZo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clinically important distinction between marginal and conditional-on-stopping risk and the model-agnostic post-hoc wrapper requiring no retraining.
pEL9WvPxZo.main_concern: Reviewers point out limited statistical novelty (a direct application of Learn-Then-Test with Holm correction), missing comparisons to recent risk-aware early-stopping baselines, and unaddressed distribution shift.

9FMfQxOc3b.one_liner: Separates reward-guided diffusion search history from winner-anchored farthest-first subset selection for diverse high-reward images.
9FMfQxOc3b.problem: Gradient-free test-time reward search for diffusion models returns redundant top-k images from its active archive while discarding distinct high-reward candidates found earlier.
9FMfQxOc3b.method: Source Portfolio Guidance (SPG) combines Trajectory Support Consolidation (TSC), which stores a persistent history of multiscale reward-driven proposals, with Anchored Support Compression (ASC), which keeps the top-reward image and applies winner-anchored farthest-first coverage over reward-qualified candidates without extra generator calls.
9FMfQxOc3b.key_idea: Maintains a persistent search archive and selects a diverse, reward-qualified output set via winner-anchored farthest-first traversal without extra diffusion evaluations.
9FMfQxOc3b.evidence: Coverage guarantees and evaluations across Stable Diffusion 1.4, 1.5, and XL on held-out prompts with same-pool selection ablations.
9FMfQxOc3b.claimed_gains: Across Stable Diffusion 1.4, 1.5, and XL, SPG improves best-of-four ImageReward by 0.105–0.176.
9FMfQxOc3b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating candidate discovery from diversity-aware finite-set selection is practical, avoids extra generator calls, and is cleanly isolated by the same-pool ablation.
9FMfQxOc3b.main_concern: Reviewers question originality since TSC stores search history and ASC is thresholded farthest-first traversal, note narrow baseline comparisons (mainly SPT) using the same search/test reward model, and flag high search compute.

wBezjNx3Pq.one_liner: Trains a single LLM with competing segment-level process rewards so reasoning explores unsafe paths while answers remain safe.
wBezjNx3Pq.problem: Safety training frequently causes over-refusal on benign prompts because models avoid exploring unsafe interpretations during safety reasoning.
wBezjNx3Pq.method: SEAR formulates safety alignment as an adversarial optimization within one chain-of-thought where a reasoning segment is rewarded for exploring unsafe strategies and an answer segment is rewarded for producing a safe final output, stabilized using dense process rewards.
wBezjNx3Pq.key_idea: Apply competing segment-level process rewards to one model so the reasoning segment explores harmful interpretations while the answer segment enforces a safe response.
wBezjNx3Pq.evidence: Experiments compare SEAR against outcome-reward baselines across controlled reward designs on safety and over-refusal evaluations.
wBezjNx3Pq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing over-refusal through exploratory harmful reasoning with separated segment-level process rewards is an interesting hypothesis addressing an important problem.
wBezjNx3Pq.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the experiments do not causally establish that harmful reasoning drives the over-refusal reduction, noting that the reward optimizes Moderation-API harmfulness rather than ambiguity resolution.

xDAUggwlh7.one_liner: Conditions rotary position embeddings on a nontextual secret key and trains models to suppress unauthorized capability execution.
xDAUggwlh7.problem: Existing model capability controls rely on external textual passwords rather than internal architectural conditions.
xDAUggwlh7.method: KeyedRoPE applies key-conditioned positional and RoPE phase transformations together with protection training that preserves task performance under the authorized key while degrading outputs under standard RoPE and incorrect keys.
xDAUggwlh7.key_idea: Condition RoPE phase and positional geometry on a compact nontextual key and train the model to perform tasks only under the authorized attention geometry.
xDAUggwlh7.evidence: Evaluations span four language models from 410M to 8B parameters and four downstream tasks, including white-box gradient geometry search and fine-tuning recovery attacks on Qwen3-4B Mobile Action.
xDAUggwlh7.claimed_gains: In the Qwen3-4B Mobile Action evaluation, full-data adaptation recovers 96.2% of pre-attack authorized utility and 92.13% of original task-adapted utility under standard RoPE.
xDAUggwlh7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that gating capabilities via key-conditioned attention geometry is an interesting alternative to textual passwords, tested across multiple model sizes and adaptive attacks.
xDAUggwlh7.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited baseline comparisons, insufficient geometric ablations, reliance on a single disclosed key, and potential collapse of the phase transform to a shared positional warp under white-box analysis.

sOVhO03Mea.one_liner: Treats prompt-derived LLM time-series forecasts as a rejectable conditional residual correction gated over a numerical predictor.
sOVhO03Mea.problem: LLM time-series forecasters couple numerical predictors with prompts generated from the same series (pseudo-multimodality), where cross-view similarity does not guarantee predictive benefit.
sOVhO03Mea.method: Conditional Incremental and Robust Fusion (CIRF) keeps the numerical forecast as default, projects out prompt components predictable from numerical features, decodes the remaining conditional residual as a candidate correction, applies it via a utility-supervised gate, and regularizes shared-input perturbation sensitivity.
sOVhO03Mea.key_idea: Remove the numerically predictable part of the prompt representation and apply the remaining conditional residual as a utility-gated correction to the default numerical forecast.
sOVhO03Mea.evidence: Experiments evaluate CIRF on nine public time-series benchmarks across six same-checkpoint routing settings, alongside randomized-model, unmatched-prompt, and Stats-MLP controls.
sOVhO03Mea.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the pseudo-multimodality framing and controlled attribution experiments are clear, scientifically meaningful, and transparently reported.
sOVhO03Mea.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical value of the language pathway and conditional residuals given that cheaper numerical or Stats-MLP baselines perform comparably and routing gains are small.

mkFY1wMIM6.one_liner: Develops a finite-net Q-learning algorithm for non-exchangeable heterogeneous mean-field control with common noise and error decompositions.
mkFY1wMIM6.problem: Cooperative reinforcement learning in large heterogeneous multi-agent populations with common noise yields infinite-dimensional population-law state spaces and kernel action spaces lacking unified finite-net guarantees.
mkFY1wMIM6.method: The authors formulate a label-preserving non-exchangeable mean-field control problem, restrict relaxed policies to Lipschitz kernels, and design a finite-net Q-learning algorithm with almost-sure convergence to the projected Bellman fixed point and finite-population performance bounds.
mkFY1wMIM6.key_idea: Restrict relaxed mean-field policies to Lipschitz kernels and run finite-net Q-learning over discretized population-law states with separate error bounds for restriction, discretization, learning, and finite-population transfer.
mkFY1wMIM6.evidence: Theoretical proofs establish uniform consistency, finite-net bias, almost-sure convergence, and finite-population bounds, complemented by congestion, cybersecurity, and linear-quadratic experiments.
mkFY1wMIM6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note a clean separation of approximation and learning error sources, uniform Lipschitz-kernel consistency, and honest experimental diagnostics.
mkFY1wMIM6.main_concern: Reviewers point out that experiments do not show a clear advantage from population-law or label conditioning over static controls, and cite incomplete finite-population bound specifications and dense notation.

rNRgtnA2k8.one_liner: Transfers external vision-language query relevance into target VLM encoders by expanding evidence seeds through internal visual attention.
rNRgtnA2k8.problem: Mapping query relevance from an external vision-language alignment model onto a target VLM's visual tokens is difficult when their vision encoders and representations differ.
rNRgtnA2k8.method: QUEST selects query-relevant Evidence Seeds using an external VLAM, expands them via internal visual attention at an intermediate target encoder layer chosen by attention distance, combines this Evidence Attention with Visual Guidance, and applies diversity-aware selection under a token budget.
rNRgtnA2k8.key_idea: Map external VLAM query relevance to target VLM visual tokens as Evidence Seeds and propagate importance through intermediate-layer visual self-attention before diversity-aware pruning.
rNRgtnA2k8.evidence: Evaluations test QUEST on LLaVA-NeXT-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B across multiple external VLAMs, token budgets, and nine VLM benchmarks.
rNRgtnA2k8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using external relevance seeds expanded via internal visual attention is a sensible, training-free way to bridge mismatched encoders in Pre-LLM visual token pruning.
rNRgtnA2k8.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains over strong baselines like SFPruner are marginal (a few tenths of a point at higher cost) and that ablations fail to isolate seed-and-expand from direct relevance interpolation or visual-only guidance.

8yE2hYe4DU.one_liner: Casts posterior-score reverse-time diffusion sampling for medical image reconstruction as a parallelizable deep equilibrium fixed-point problem.
8yE2hYe4DU.problem: Score-based generative models for medical imaging inverse problems struggle to incorporate physical measurement posteriors accurately and suffer from slow sequential sampling.
8yE2hYe4DU.method: DEQ-Solver builds a measurement-conditioned neural vector field to estimate the posterior score and uses an implicit backward Euler discretization to cast the entire reverse-time trajectory as a global fixed-point problem solved jointly in parallel.
8yE2hYe4DU.key_idea: Formulate implicit backward-Euler reverse-time posterior score dynamics as a global fixed-point equilibrium problem to solve all trajectory states jointly in parallel.
8yE2hYe4DU.evidence: Experiments evaluate reconstruction quality and sampling speed across medical imaging modalities including Magnetic Particle Imaging against accelerated score-based samplers.
8yE2hYe4DU.claimed_gains: DEQ-Solver achieves a 7.3x speedup over other accelerated samplers in Magnetic Particle Imaging while achieving superior reconstruction quality.
8yE2hYe4DU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find casting diffusion posterior sampling as a global fixed-point problem for trajectory-level parallelization an interesting direction for accelerating reconstruction.
8yE2hYe4DU.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing related-work comparisons (e.g., optimal posterior covariance, DAPS, PnP-DM, parallel/flow samplers) and unclear details on how the measurement-conditioned posterior score estimator is trained.

73o2bc3VP2.one_liner: Audits synthetic pre-pretraining under compute-matched natural-language budgets and attributes prior gains partly to initialization.
73o2bc3VP2.problem: Prior claims that pre-pretraining on synthetic non-natural-language data improves language models rarely test compute-matched allocations against natural-language training or control for weight initialization.
73o2bc3VP2.method: The authors conduct compute-matched and additive-compute empirical studies across four synthetic pre-pretraining curricula (k-Dyck, neural cellular automata, declarative reference corpora, and code), three training regimes, initialization variations, and data interleaving.
73o2bc3VP2.key_idea: Compare synthetic pre-pretraining against compute-matched natural-language training and alternative weight initializations across data-constrained, unconstrained, and high token-to-parameter regimes.
73o2bc3VP2.evidence: Experiments cover models up to 881M parameters on 50B tokens, 100M-token data-constrained corpora, and an NCA reproduction averaged across three seeds with separate hyperparameter tuning.
73o2bc3VP2.claimed_gains: In an NCA reproduction, the authors recover a 5.4% perplexity improvement from PPT under the original initialization scheme, while additive-compute PPT gains disappear by 1B natural-language tokens.
73o2bc3VP2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-controlled compute-matched empirical study, separate hyperparameter tuning, and coverage across multiple regimes including interleaving.
73o2bc3VP2.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the initialization attribution is overstated relative to additive-compute results and reused hyperparameters, and note limited statistical testing with three seeds.

MwT46VXMCc.one_liner: Constructs an unbiased pairwise value-gap estimator from comparison run lengths and pairs it with online-to-nonconvex conversion for nonsmooth optimization.
MwT46VXMCc.problem: Minimizing nonsmooth nonconvex Lipschitz functions from noisy pairwise comparisons lacks unbiased value-gap estimators and tight complexity characterizations for Goldstein stationarity.
MwT46VXMCc.method: The authors repeatedly compare a pair (x, y) until the outcome flips and return a scaled partial sum of inverse-link expansion coefficients (harmonic numbers for the logistic link) to obtain an exact unbiased estimator of f(y) - f(x) with finite expected cost and bounded second moment. Combining this with randomized smoothing and online-to-nonconvex conversion yields Goldstein-stationarity complexity bounds.
MwT46VXMCc.key_idea: Queries noisy pairwise comparisons until an outcome flip and sums inverse-link series coefficients over the run length for an unbiased gap estimator in online-to-nonconvex optimization.
MwT46VXMCc.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower comparison-complexity bounds for lens-analytic links (logistic, probit, cauchit) plus small-scale numerical experiments (e.g., Chebyshev-Rosenbrock).
MwT46VXMCc.claimed_gains: Achieves (delta, epsilon)-Goldstein stationarity with O(d(1 + d C_link / kappa^2) L^2 Delta_f / (delta epsilon^3)) comparisons and 1 + 1/(1 - alpha) expected comparisons per gap estimate.
MwT46VXMCc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the simple, truncation-free run-length unbiased gap estimator and its clean theoretical integration with randomized smoothing and Goldstein-stationarity bounds.
MwT46VXMCc.main_concern: Reviewers point out a gap between the dimension-dependent upper bound and narrow-regime lower bound, lack of explicit inverse-link coefficients for non-logistic links, and experiments where biased plug-in estimators outperform the unbiased method.

YYLLBLGwue.one_liner: Characterizes local averaging, parallel particle propagation, and Best-of-N selection in training-free guided diffusion/flow sampling and exposes diagnostic failures.
YYLLBLGwue.problem: Test-time scaling strategies for training-free guided generative models frequently fail or degrade outputs inconsistently across samplers, and standard diagnostics like ESS or rank agreement can mislead.
YYLLBLGwue.method: The authors unify three scaling axes—averaging K local draws, propagating P parallel particles, and selecting among N final samples—using bias-variance, Feynman-Kac, and order-statistic analyses to pinpoint what extra compute refines and where scaling stalls. They construct matched counterexamples showing that conventional summaries like ESS and Kendall's tau fail to predict utility gains.
YYLLBLGwue.key_idea: Analyzes K-draw averaging, P-particle propagation, and Best-of-N selection via bias-variance, Feynman-Kac, and order-statistic identities with counterexamples to ESS and rank-correlation diagnostics.
YYLLBLGwue.evidence: Theoretical propositions/counterexamples and empirical studies across 18 checkpoints and 29 training-free guidance settings.
YYLLBLGwue.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad 18-checkpoint empirical survey and exact counterexamples demonstrating that ESS and Kendall's tau cannot determine scaling utility.
YYLLBLGwue.main_concern: Reviewers note that the theoretical framework largely formalizes standard statistical identities without delivering actionable criteria, better estimators, or performance guarantees for practitioners.

KXegdbwovc.one_liner: Compiles egocentric video annotations into restorable symbolic environments for branching recovery SFT and continuation-comparison RL on compact planners.
KXegdbwovc.problem: Real-world egocentric demonstration videos show only single nominal trajectories, leaving alternative choices and error recovery unexplored for long-horizon planning.
KXegdbwovc.method: EgoVine compiles annotated egocentric videos into executable, restorable symbolic environments where a compact planner branches from decision states to explore alternatives and failures. It jointly trains action generation, consequence prediction, candidate comparison, and verified failure recovery (Union) alongside continuation-based RL updates.
KXegdbwovc.key_idea: Branches from decision states in video-compiled restorable symbolic environments to generate verified failure-recovery targets and continuation-comparison policy updates.
KXegdbwovc.evidence: Evaluated 0.5B and 1.5B planners on a shared benchmark of Main and longer composed household planning tasks against Flash LLM baselines.
KXegdbwovc.claimed_gains: EgoVine-1.5B achieves 81.8% success on Main planning tasks and 66.7% on longer task compositions, outperforming evaluated Flash LLM baselines on both.
KXegdbwovc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the motivation of expanding fixed demonstrations through branching execution and verified recovery in restorable environments, noting strong gains over Flash baselines.
KXegdbwovc.main_concern: Reviewers highlight heavy dependence on costly annotated symbolic environments (Ego2World), evaluation restricted to self-constructed text-symbolic benchmarks overlapping with training worlds, marginal RL gain over recovery SFT, and unexplained recipe differences between 0.5B and 1.5B models.

63akxy1NZD.one_liner: Provides a programmable multi-agent coding runtime with event-stream Adherence tracking to audit whether declared team organizations are actually followed.
63akxy1NZD.problem: Multi-agent coding evaluations assume configured team structures are faithfully executed, obscuring whether observed gains come from collaboration or unmeasured behavioral and system differences.
63akxy1NZD.method: OpenCollab unifies declarative organization design with a controlled shared runtime that enforces role, tool, messaging, and token budgets while logging fine-grained role-attributed event streams. It defines an Adherence metric to measure how faithfully agents realize the declared organization across configurations.
63akxy1NZD.key_idea: Enforces programmable role/tool/budget boundaries in a shared coding runtime and logs role-attributed event streams to quantify organizational Adherence.
63akxy1NZD.evidence: Evaluated organizational Adherence across model, tool, budget, context, and topology shifts, plus coding benchmark runs (SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.1, DeepSWE) against Mini-SWE-agent, Codex CLI, and Claude Code.
63akxy1NZD.claimed_gains: Changing model, tools, budget, context, or topology shifts Adherence from 47.2% to 97.2% relative to a reference team.
63akxy1NZD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the auditable runtime infrastructure and the finding that declared multi-agent organizations frequently diverge from runtime behavior.
63akxy1NZD.main_concern: Reviewers find the leaderboard claims unsupported (single model/run, subset of SWE-bench Pro, 1-task margin), note missing compute-matched single-agent baselines to separate collaboration from extra compute, and flag confounded single-dimension ablations.

auOviHWaS9.one_liner: Prefills compacted summaries while relocating cached keys and preserving values of retained messages to accelerate agent prefill after context compaction.
auOviHWaS9.problem: Long-running agents compact conversations by summarizing older messages and retaining recent ones, causing expensive redundant prefill recomputation of retained history.
auOviHWaS9.method: The paper studies position-corrected KV-cache reuse after context compaction: it prefills only the new summary, shifts positional encodings on retained keys, and preserves retained values without recomputing them against the new summary, measuring both recovery speedup and behavioral drift.
auOviHWaS9.key_idea: Prefills only the compaction summary while relocating retained cached keys and keeping cached values, trading exact re-conditioning for faster warm recovery.
auOviHWaS9.evidence: Benchmarked on twelve compaction boundaries with Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B, three controlled live agent continuations, and six Qwen3-8B Astropy semantic-replay boundaries.
auOviHWaS9.claimed_gains: Measures a 10.98x geometric-mean warm-recovery speedup on a twelve-boundary Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B benchmark and 1.56-8.56x local recovery latency reduction across three controlled agent boundaries (with one continuation failing seven additional preservation tests).
auOviHWaS9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree redundant prefill of retained messages after context compaction is a real bottleneck and appreciate documenting substantial warm-recovery speedups alongside concrete behavioral costs.
auOviHWaS9.main_concern: Reviewers note speed and quality are evaluated across mismatched models/runs (Mistral vs. Qwen), lack comparisons against selective recomputation or residual-correction baselines, and provide limited end-to-end task-success evidence (46 tasks).

gpqH98THyv.one_liner: Jointly optimizes quantization formats, mixed-precision allocation, and codebook compression for accuracy, storage, and throughput on a many-core edge accelerator.
gpqH98THyv.problem: Edge AI accelerators cannot refresh silicon as fast as models evolve, and standard post-training quantization minimizes weight error without accounting for hardware unpacking, dequantization, and runtime bottlenecks.
gpqH98THyv.method: The authors treat post-training quantization as a full inference-stack optimization over standard (MXFP, NVFP) and custom block formats, group sizes, and hierarchical scales. They characterize hardware fetching/dequantization costs and apply output-sensitivity mixed-precision allocation and codebook quantization across dense and MoE models.
gpqH98THyv.key_idea: Prunes candidate quantization formats via hardware unpacking/dequantization profiling and allocates mixed-precision/codebook formats under joint storage and decode-time constraints.
gpqH98THyv.evidence: End-to-end hardware measurements and accuracy benchmarks across dense and MoE models from 4B to 35B parameters on a many-core edge inference accelerator.
gpqH98THyv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the detailed hardware characterization linking weight fetching, unpacking, and dequantization costs to real throughput across dense and MoE models.
gpqH98THyv.main_concern: All three reviewers note that the dual-constraint allocator's incremental value is not isolated—at K-quant budgets the decode-time constraint is inactive (yielding identical assignments to storage-only allocation), and ablations rely on predicted objectives rather than measured accuracy.

0UvUvv9QZ3.one_liner: Diagnoses extrapolative and compositional OOD generalization gaps in single- and multi-teacher on-policy distillation via update-geometry analysis.
0UvUvv9QZ3.problem: Near-perfect in-distribution fidelity in on-policy distillation (OPD) and multi-teacher OPD (MOPD) can mask incomplete capability consolidation and OOD forgetting beyond the supervised distribution.
0UvUvv9QZ3.method: The authors evaluate OPD and MOPD across synthetic, extrapolative, and compositional multi-domain tasks on Qwen3 models, analyze teacher capability and data-coverage bottlenecks, compare parameter-update geometry against RL baselines, and propose geometry-based patching to mitigate OOD degradation.
0UvUvv9QZ3.key_idea: Measures IND-vs-OOD and compositional gaps in OPD/MOPD, links them to teacher capability, data coverage, and compact shared update geometry, and applies geometry-based patching.
0UvUvv9QZ3.evidence: Synthetic reasoning study plus real-world extrapolative and compositional experiments across math, coding, agent, and long-context benchmarks using Qwen3 models.
0UvUvv9QZ3.claimed_gains: OPD and MOPD reach 96.04-102.73% of teachers' mean IND scores yet stay 2.45-16.25% below the base model on OOD tasks, while MOPD improves IND by 0.48-22.46% over base but trails best teachers by 18.19-24.34% on composed tasks.
0UvUvv9QZ3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree studying whether on-policy distillation transfers true generalization versus in-distribution behavior across compositional domains is timely and well-motivated.
0UvUvv9QZ3.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the circular IND/OOD benchmark split (defined by post-training teacher performance), single-run experiments with small gaps, and unclear isolation of OPD-specific failure from narrow-distribution training.

gF07Eukddi.one_liner: Scores realized quantization residuals with matrix-free block Fisher products to solve mixed-precision integer-byte allocation for Mamba checkpoints.
gF07Eukddi.problem: Diagonal sensitivity metrics for mixed-precision quantization discard signed coordinate cross-terms of deterministic rounding residuals, misallocating scarce high-precision bytes in state-space models.
gF07Eukddi.method: BlockFAMQ computes matrix-free empirical Fisher scores from squared per-token gradient-residual products for realized rounding candidates and solves the resulting multiple-choice knapsack problem under a complete-checkpoint byte budget.
gF07Eukddi.key_idea: Prices realized quantization candidates using matrix-free squared per-token gradient-residual products (capturing cross-terms) within a complete-checkpoint byte-budget solver.
gF07Eukddi.evidence: Controlled candidate-bank evaluations on Mamba-1 (130M-2.8B), Mamba-2 2.7B, Falcon-Mamba 7B, Pythia-1.4B, and Llama-3.2-3B on WikiText-2 NLL and six downstream tasks.
gF07Eukddi.claimed_gains: On Mamba-1 (130M-2.8B), BlockFAMQ lowers WikiText-2 NLL over diagonal allocation by 0.218 at 2.5 bits, 0.026 at 4.0 bits, and 0.009 at 4.5 bits; at 3.5 bits it improves six-task accuracy by 2.08 points and recovers 65.7-80.1% of the NLL gap to FP32, while packed W4A8 retains 96.8-97.7% of Quamba2 decode throughput.
gF07Eukddi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clear theoretical motivation for signed residual cross-terms, the matrix-free formulation, and the clean controlled allocator comparison on a shared candidate bank.
gF07Eukddi.main_concern: Reviewers point out high calibration cost (115 A100 GPU-hours for Mamba-1 1.4B), gains vanishing at practical 4.0-4.5 bits while direct KL beats BlockFAMQ at 3.0 bits, heavy reliance on older Mamba-1 models, and missing external baselines.

MYWxmjoGDX.one_liner: Rehearses features before adapters and rebuilds or transports class statistics under the updated global encoder for federated class-incremental learning.
MYWxmjoGDX.problem: Under asynchronous class exposure in federated class-incremental learning, fixed stored memories become stale, bypass trainable adapters, or use incompatible encoder coordinates as representations evolve.
MYWxmjoGDX.method: The authors propose Projected Rehearsal Orchestration (PRO), which replays current and stored evidence before the adapter and rebuilds available class statistics under the aggregated global encoder. For unavailable classes, PRO-MAX estimates local feature drift from current calibration data and aggregates client estimates via support weights.
MYWxmjoGDX.key_idea: Rehearse evidence before the adapter, rebuild class statistics under the aggregated global encoder, and transport missing class memories via support-weighted local drift estimates.
MYWxmjoGDX.evidence: Evaluated across six image, text, and graph benchmarks over five seeds with transport and replay-source control ablations.
MYWxmjoGDX.claimed_gains: PRO-MAX achieves the highest reported mean final accuracy among evaluated methods on all six streams.
MYWxmjoGDX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing heterogeneous FCIL around asynchronous class exposure and co-evolving memory is useful and backed by extensive multi-modality experiments and controls.
MYWxmjoGDX.main_concern: Reviewers question methodological novelty relative to existing Gaussian feature replay and drift-compensation methods, and note unmatched replay budgets and unmeasured ACE metrics.

c7iYch4QMe.one_liner: Establishes latent SCM isomorphism conditions for counterfactual identifiability and builds FlowSCM to recover latent causal models.
c7iYch4QMe.problem: It is unclear when latent structural causal models learned from factual data agree on counterfactual predictions.
c7iYch4QMe.method: The authors define counterfactual identifiability under a single intervention correspondence, prove that latent SCM isomorphism implies it given an exogenous-modulating auxiliary variable and one hard intervention per non-root endogenous variable, and build the FlowSCM estimator.
c7iYch4QMe.key_idea: Use an exogenous-modulating auxiliary variable and single hard interventions per non-root endogenous node to achieve latent SCM isomorphism and counterfactual identifiability.
c7iYch4QMe.evidence: Supported by theoretical identifiability proofs for counterfactuals and natural direct/indirect effects, plus experiments with FlowSCM on synthetic and image data.
c7iYch4QMe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing counterfactual identifiability for latent SCMs is an important direction beyond standard representation identifiability.
c7iYch4QMe.main_concern: Reviewers find the assumptions of multi-regime exogenous variability and hard interventions on every non-root latent variable too restrictive for practice, and note the unknown intervention correspondence weakens the headline claim.

5zHH8quSC9.one_liner: Audits test-time compute oracles by separating retrospective coverage, expected-action value, split-selected value, and held-out routing policy value.
5zHH8quSC9.problem: Test-time compute studies often report retrospective oracle coverage, which overstates the achievable decision-time policy value of selecting stochastic actions before outcomes are known.
5zHH8quSC9.method: The authors formalize retrospective coverage, expected-action oracle, finite-replication split-selected value, and held-out policy value, and audit empirical gaps under product coupling across repeated stochastic prompt rollouts and four held-out router families.
5zHH8quSC9.key_idea: Separate retrospective outcome-dependent coverage from expected-action, finite-sample split-selected, and held-out policy values under explicit outcome coupling.
5zHH8quSC9.evidence: Evaluated on 771 model-problem states from three open models on MATH-500 and GPQA-Diamond using five prompt actions with 16 outcomes per action (extended to 64 on GPQA).
5zHH8quSC9.claimed_gains: Retrospective coverage exceeds split-selected value by 4.41 percentage points on MATH ([3.63, 5.26]) and 11.73 points on GPQA ([10.34, 13.17]), leaving an 11.60-point GPQA gap at 64 outcomes, while no held-out router passes multiplicity-adjusted gains.
5zHH8quSC9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly separating retrospective coverage, expected-action value, finite-panel selection, and deployable routing value clarifies oracle evaluation.
5zHH8quSC9.main_concern: Reviewers view the theoretical propositions as standard statistics already reflected in pass@k versus pass@1, and note that finite-sample selection regret confounds the measured gap to the population oracle.

AkYCyaF50U.one_liner: Compresses video-LLM tokens via greedy attention-weighted spatiotemporal tree partitioning and importance-weighted feature pooling under a fixed budget.
AkYCyaF50U.problem: Video-LLMs incur high computational cost from dense visual tokens and must decide where to allocate a fixed token budget across temporal versus spatial resolution.
AkYCyaF50U.method: DART partitions the video feature volume into contiguous spatiotemporal regions using a greedy planner that chooses temporal, spatial, or spatiotemporal splits maximizing attention-weighted reconstruction-error reduction per token, with content-dependent boundaries for temporal splits (Adaptive-T), followed by importance-weighted pooling before LLM prefilling.
AkYCyaF50U.key_idea: Greedily refine spatiotemporal video regions by maximum attention-weighted reconstruction-error reduction per token and pool each region before prefilling.
AkYCyaF50U.evidence: Evaluated training-free across four video-understanding benchmarks on 0.5B and 7B video-LLMs with component ablations.
AkYCyaF50U.claimed_gains: Averaged over four video-understanding benchmarks, DART retains 101.2% and 102.7% of full-token baseline accuracy.
AkYCyaF50U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that DART offers a well-motivated, training-free, query-independent reconstruction formulation for adaptive spatiotemporal token allocation.
AkYCyaF50U.main_concern: Reviewers note missing end-to-end latency and compression-overhead evaluations, modest ablation gains from Adaptive-T and joint splitting, and limited novelty over prior structured tree-pruning methods.

9P45y2Yyo1.one_liner: Trains an early-stopping predictor directly on stop-harm events and certifies request-level lost-correct risk thresholds for reasoning models.
9P45y2Yyo1.problem: Existing early-stopping predictors for reasoning models supervise proxy targets like current-answer correctness or stability, which mismatch the certified lost-correct risk.
9P45y2Yyo1.method: StopHarm trains a lightweight predictor offline on paired checkpoint-stopping and full-reasoning outcomes to predict stop-harm probability directly, and halts online generation when predicted stop harm falls below a threshold calibrated for request-level lost-correct risk.
9P45y2Yyo1.key_idea: Directly supervise a lightweight checkpoint predictor on paired stop-harm outcomes and halt generation when predicted harm falls below a certified risk threshold.
9P45y2Yyo1.evidence: Supported by an information-loss proof for proxy targets and experiments across three reasoning models and five benchmarks.
9P45y2Yyo1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that directly supervising stop harm to align training with the certified stopping loss is simple, well motivated, and theoretically justified.
9P45y2Yyo1.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty and offline labeling cost, uncompetitive accuracy-token tradeoffs on MATH500 against baselines like BLADE and LYNX, and broken i.i.d. certification assumptions when transferring from MATH to other benchmarks.

hrF0AjBkeM.one_liner: Generates sparse counterfactual explanations for signed graph link-sign prediction by decoupling differentiable edge existence and polarity perturbations.
hrF0AjBkeM.problem: Counterfactual explanation methods for graphs overlook signed graphs, where link predictions depend jointly on edge existence and positive/negative polarity.
hrF0AjBkeM.method: CoSG decouples edge polarity from edge existence to enable differentiable edge-removal and sign-flip perturbations, and trains an amortized model-agnostic explainer across instances to balance counterfactual validity and sparsity.
hrF0AjBkeM.key_idea: Decouple edge existence and polarity in a differentiable perturbation parameterization to train an amortized counterfactual explainer supporting deletions and sign flips.
hrF0AjBkeM.evidence: Evaluated on link-sign prediction across three signed-graph datasets (including BitcoinOTC, Twitter, and Epinions with SGCN) and perturbation-restricted ablations.
hrF0AjBkeM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that counterfactual explanations for signed graphs are a relevant direction and that decoupling existence from polarity cleanly models sign flips.
hrF0AjBkeM.main_concern: Reviewers point out that learned baselines can only delete edges while CoSG also flips signs, confounding the method's contribution with access to a stronger perturbation space.

wMschf41Pm.one_liner: TextCanvasBench evaluates text-to-image models on 1,600 long-text, multi-region layouts across macro image and micro text-block dimensions.
wMschf41Pm.problem: Existing text-rendering benchmarks cover only short text and aggregate OCR scores, failing to evaluate long-form text, multi-region layouts, and block-level style or semantic relations.
wMschf41Pm.method: TextCanvasBench contains 1,600 specification-guided samples across 8 domains and 38 subcategories (from short labels to >1,000 characters) with annotated text blocks and roles. It scores generations across four macro-to-micro dimensions: glyph quality, text accuracy, layout/style fidelity, and block-level semantic alignment.
wMschf41Pm.key_idea: Pairs 1,600 long-text multi-region layout specifications with a four-dimension macro-to-micro rubric evaluating glyph, text, layout/style, and block-level semantics.
wMschf41Pm.evidence: Benchmarks open- and closed-source T2I models across 8 domains and 38 subcategories and reports Spearman correlations with human rankings.
wMschf41Pm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating long-text, multi-region T2I rendering across four decomposed dimensions is practically relevant and covers realistic domains comprehensively.
wMschf41Pm.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of human-evaluation protocol details (annotator count, sample size, criteria, inter-annotator agreement) needed to validate the claimed human-ranking correlations, plus minor dataset count inconsistencies.

lJj9QgYW2w.one_liner: ESPTQ post-training ternarizes both LLM weights and KV cache into a unified two-plane format capping multiplications at 1.5625%.
lJj9QgYW2w.problem: Weight-only ternary quantization removes linear-layer multipliers but leaves floating-point per-element multiplications in attention's QK^T and PV products.
lJj9QgYW2w.method: ESPTQ applies a learnable butterfly rotation per 128-column weight group and a rate-distortion criterion to assign a sparse second ternary plane to selected weights, while using static tables for KV-cache offsets and V scaling. Both weights and KV cache share a ternary format capping residual multiplications at 2 per 128-element reduction.
lJj9QgYW2w.key_idea: Quantizes both weights (with butterfly rotation and sparse second ternary plane) and KV cache (with static tables) into one ternary format capping multiplications at 2/128.
lJj9QgYW2w.evidence: Evaluated across LLaMA-2, LLaMA-3.2, Qwen2.5, and Qwen3 models using serialized effective bits per weight (including auxiliary metadata), perplexity, and CSR accuracy.
lJj9QgYW2w.claimed_gains: Caps residual multiplications at 2 per 128-element reduction (1.5625%).
lJj9QgYW2w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate extending ternary computation from weights to KV cache in a compatible format and accounting honestly for serialized effective bit-widths including metadata.
lJj9QgYW2w.main_concern: Reviewers note the absence of real hardware latency/speedup measurements, missing low-bit KV-cache baselines and hard reasoning/generation tasks, and incomplete ablations isolating rate-distortion selection.

FwzDg8qGWN.one_liner: EFG removes the visual encoder and feeds raw patch-embedded pixel tokens directly into an LLM for synthetic image detection and explanation.
FwzDg8qGWN.problem: Visual encoders in VLM-based synthetic image detectors compress images into high-level semantics, discarding low-level forensic artifacts needed for detection and explanation.
FwzDg8qGWN.method: Encoder-Free Forensic Guard (EFG) replaces the pretrained visual encoder with a lightweight patch embedding layer that feeds raw pixel-level tokens directly into an LLM backbone (adapted from NEO), jointly predicting authenticity and natural-language forensic explanations.
FwzDg8qGWN.key_idea: Drops the pretrained visual encoder and feeds raw patch-embedded pixel tokens directly into an LLM to preserve low-level forensic signals.
FwzDg8qGWN.evidence: Evaluated on FakeClue, LOKI, and DMImage benchmarks, including four image-degradation conditions and qualitative explanation examples.
FwzDg8qGWN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that encoder-induced loss of low-level artifacts is a relevant bottleneck and that an encoder-free native VLM formulation for forensic detection is an interesting direction.
FwzDg8qGWN.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing recent forensic and VLM baselines, lack of controlled same-backbone ablations isolating encoder removal from backbone/training differences, and unverified faithfulness of generated explanations.

9XBEOBZIzr.one_liner: A solver-free generator constructs target-aligned labeled SAT/UNSAT formulas directly, paired with an LP-residual message-passing GNN (LPGNN).
9XBEOBZIzr.problem: Scaling neural SAT learning is bottlenecked by invoking SAT solvers to label generated formulas as problem sizes grow.
9XBEOBZIzr.method: The authors propose a target-aware, solver-free SAT generator that constructs labeled SAT and UNSAT instances matching structural properties of a target benchmark without solver verification, alongside LPGNN, which injects linear-programming constraint-violation residuals into GNN message passing.
9XBEOBZIzr.key_idea: Constructs target-matched labeled SAT/UNSAT formulas without a solver and augments GNN message passing with LP constraint-violation residuals.
9XBEOBZIzr.evidence: Evaluates generator speed, summary graph statistics, and downstream GNN SAT prediction accuracy.
9XBEOBZIzr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that solver-free generation of benchmark-aligned labeled SAT instances addresses an important scalability bottleneck in neural combinatorial learning.
9XBEOBZIzr.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing comparisons against planted-SAT and synthetic SAT dataset baselines (NeuroSAT, G4SATBench, HardSATGEN, HardCore), lack of deeper topological or non-random SAT evaluation, and experimental clarity issues.
